pages.title: Getting started
pages.summary: Signing in, the menu, Home tasks, favourites, and signing out.
pages.text: Signing in 1. Open the ERP's address in your browser Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox . 2. On Sign In , enter: Corporate ID : your organisation's ID, given by your administrator; Email address and Password : your own ERP account. 3. Select Sign In . You arrive at the menu the Module Hierarchy . If the ERP says your account is inactive or not configured, ask your administrator: an account must be active and assigned to at least one company and role. Forgot your password? On the sign in page, open Forgot Password , enter your email address and select Send Reset Link . A link to set a new password arrives by email. Once signed in, you can change your password at any time from the user menu your name, top right → Change Password . The menu The menu is a tree of areas Finance, Procurement, Inventory and so on . You see only the screens your role allows. Select an area to open it; select a screen to start working in it. Search modules top bar : type part of a screen's name to filter the menu. Enter opens the screen when only one matches; Esc clears the search. The double arrow button expands or collapses the whole tree. Inside a screen, Back to Hierarchy returns to the menu. If you have unsaved changes, the ERP asks before leaving. Favourites Put the screens you use most at the top of the menu: user menu → Configure Favourites , select the star next to each screen you want, then Done . Home tasks The Tasks button top bar shows what is waiting for you, with a count. Select a line to open that document. What you may see, depending on your role: Block What it means Your Pending Approvals Documents waiting for your approval. Rejected — Needs Your Resubmission Your documents an approver rejected, with the reason. Correct and submit again. Ready for You to Act On Approved documents your team follows up for example, raising the purchase order for an approved requisition . The teams are set in Approval Configuration. My Drafts — Not Yet Submitted or Posted Documents you saved as drafts. Post dated Cheques Due to Clear Cheques whose date has come. Recurring Journal Entries Due to Post Recurring entries whose date has come. Company / Employee Documents Expiring Licences, contracts or employee documents near or past expiry. Employee Requests Waiting for You Employees' queries, loan requests and claims to handle. How approvals work is explained in Approvals approvals.html . The user menu Select your name top right for: My Portal : your own leave, payslips and requests, when your ERP user is linked to an employee record; Light mode / Dark mode ; Configure Favourites ; Refresh : reloads the menu after an administrator changed it or your rights ; Change Password ; Log Out . Help The Help button top bar opens this help in a new tab. Inside a screen, it opens that screen's page directly. Signing out, and the automatic sign out Use Log Out in the user menu when you finish, especially on a shared computer. After 10 minutes without activity the ERP warns you, and signs you out 30 seconds later unless you select Stay Signed In . Anything not saved is lost, so save drafts as you go. Next Working with screens working with screens.html : dates, drafts and posting, Copy to Excel, printing, supporting documents, closed months. Approvals approvals.html .

pages.title: Working with screens
pages.summary: What every screen has in common: companies, dates, drafts and posting, messages, Copy to Excel, printing, attachments and closed months.
pages.text: Company first The ERP holds several companies. Most screens start with a Company choice; you see only the companies assigned to you. When you have only one, it is chosen for you. Lists, numbers and reports always belong to the company chosen. Dates and periods Dates show as dd/mm/yyyy 31/12/2026 and months as Sep 2026 , everywhere: on screen, in print and in what you copy to Excel. To enter a date, use the date field's calendar. Drafts, submitting and posting Entry screens journals, invoices, receipts and so on follow the same steps: 1. New opens an empty document. Fill the header company, date, party and the lines. 2. Save Draft keeps your work without any effect on the books or stock. Drafts appear in Home tasks under My Drafts , and you can change or delete them. 3. Submit or Post : where an approval is set up for that document, Submit sends it to the approver see Approvals approvals.html ; otherwise Post records it: the accounting entry and any stock movement are made, and the document gets its number. 4. A posted document cannot be edited. To correct it, Reverse it a mirror entry, dated in an open month and enter it again. The list on each entry screen shows documents by status; search and open any of them. Messages and questions Messages, confirmations "Post this document?" and questions for example a reason for a reversal appear in a box inside the ERP. Read them before choosing: Cancel always leaves things as they were. Copy to Excel and printing Copy on lists and reports copies the table; paste it into Excel and each value lands in its own cell. Print prints the report or document without the menus and buttons. To keep a PDF, choose "Save as PDF" as the printer. Supporting documents Entry screens have a Supporting documents section: Add files to keep the vendor's bill, a delivery note or a receipt with the document. Files are stored in the company's document storage, and anyone who can open the document can open its files. Closed months Finance closes each month after its checks Period Closing . Once a month is closed, nothing can be posted, reversed or approved with a date in it; the ERP says which month is closed. Use a date in an open month, or ask someone with the reopen right to reopen the month. Drilling down and going back Reports link to their detail a Trial Balance line to its ledger, a ledger line to its document . Use Back to … on the opened screen to return to the report where you left it. Saving your place The ERP signs you out after 10 minutes without activity with a warning . Save drafts as you go on long entries.

pages.title: Approvals
pages.summary: How documents are submitted, approved, rejected and delegated.
pages.text: When a document needs approval An administrator decides, per document type and company, whether documents need approval and by whom Approval Configuration . Rules can depend on the amount, and a document can need several approvers one after another. When a rule applies, Submit sends the document for approval instead of posting it. Approving 1. Your pending approvals appear in Home tasks under Your Pending Approvals . 2. Select one to open the document. Check it, and its attachments. 3. Choose Approve , or Reject with a reason. A reason is required to reject. When the last approver approves, the document is posted or, for an order or a request, becomes approved for the next step . Where a follow up team is set in Approval Configuration for example Procurement for approved requisitions , the document appears in that team's Home tasks under Ready for You to Act On . Rejected documents A rejected document returns to its submitter, with the reason, under Rejected — Needs Your Resubmission . Correct it and submit it again. Following a document Approval Tracker shows where every submitted document is: who has approved it, who it is waiting for, and since when. When an approver is away From Approval Tracker, an approver can delegate their own pending approvals, and an administrator can delegate anyone's, to another user who has access to that screen and company. A reason is required for example "On annual leave" ; who delegated, to whom and when is recorded. Closed months An approval that would post into a closed month is refused; see Working with screens working with screens.html closed months .

pages.title: Chart of Accounts
pages.summary: The list of accounts every entry posts to: heads and postable accounts, types, codes, and shared accounts.
pages.text: Chart of Accounts What it is for Every amount the ERP records lands on an account in the Chart of Accounts COA . The COA is a tree: header accounts group others for example "Current Assets" , and postable accounts receive journal lines for example "Bank — Main Account" . Before you start You need the Chart of Accounts right for your role Roles & Permissions . Decide which accounts are for one company and which are shared by all companies for example a common expense list . Step by step Add an account 1. Open Chart of Accounts and select Add Account . 2. Choose the Parent Account the head it sits under . Choose "None" to start a new top level group. 3. Enter the Name and choose the Type : Asset, Liability, Equity, Revenue, Cost of Goods Sold or Operating Expense. The normal balance debit or credit follows from the type. 4. Choose Postable if journal lines may post to it; leave it unticked for a header. 5. Choose the Company , or Shared All Companies . 6. For a header, you can set the Cash Flow Category Operating, Investing, Financing ; the accounts beneath it follow it in the Cash Flow Statement. 7. Select Save Account . The code is given automatically: the next number under the parent. Find accounts Filter by company, type, status, or "Postable only". Choosing a company shows its own accounts and the shared ones; "Shared All Companies " shows only shared ones. Move an account to another head Change its Parent Account and save. The account gets the next code under the new head, only if it has never been used . Once anything has posted to it or a document refers to it , the move is refused: create a new account under the right head, move the balance with a journal entry journal entries.html , and set the old one Inactive. Retire an account Set its Status to Inactive . It stays in the history and reports but can't be used in new entries. Good to know Some accounts are control accounts , kept by their own screens: each vendor's payables and each customer's receivables account in the Vendor and Customer masters , and each item's inventory account. Lines on a party's control account must name the party; see Paying and allocating payments and allocation.html . Cash accounts have codes starting 10 , bank accounts 11 ; Cash and Bank Transactions offers only those as the cash or bank side.

pages.title: Currency Configuration
pages.summary: The currencies list and the default (functional) currency every entry is recorded in.
pages.text: Currency Configuration What it is for Sets the default functional currency the books are kept in. Every journal entry, invoice and report is in that currency; entry screens show it in their read only Currency field. Before you start Only users with Currency Configuration rights normally Admin can change it. Set it once, before the first entry. Step by step 1. Open Currency Configuration and select Add Currency . 2. Enter the Code ISO 4217 , for example AED or USD , the Name and the Symbol . 3. Tick Set as default functional currency for the one the books use. 4. Save. Only one active currency is the default. Good to know The ERP records amounts in the default currency only; there are no exchange rates. Enter foreign currency documents at their value in the default currency. Changing the default later does not convert anything already posted, so choose it before going live.

pages.title: Opening Balances
pages.summary: Bring a company's position on its go-live date into the ERP: the trial balance, opening stock and unpaid invoices.
pages.text: Opening Balances What it is for When a company starts using the ERP, its balances from the old system are brought in once, dated the day before go live go live 1 January → opening date 31 December . Three kinds, each on its own tab: GL : the trial balance every account except the control accounts ; Stock : quantity and unit cost per item and warehouse; Open Invoices : each vendor's and customer's unpaid documents and advances, so statements, aging and payment allocation work from day one. Before you start Opening Balances is for Admin users. An Equity account for Opening Balance Clearing for example "Opening Balance Clearing" . Items, warehouses, vendors and customers already set up Master Data Import helps . Step by step 1. Choose the Company , set the Opening date and the Opening Balance Clearing account , and select Save setup . 2. On a tab, select Copy headers or Copy headers with a sample row , paste into Excel, fill it in, then copy the rows and paste them into the grid. 3. Select Check . Every problem is listed by row and column an unknown account, a missing batch number, a document entered twice… . Fix them in Excel and paste again. 4. When the check is clean, select Post . All rows post together, or none. 5. Repeat for the other tabs. When all three are in, the Clearing balance shown must be zero : then the GL, stock and open invoices agree. What each tab takes Tab Columns required ones marked on the screen GL Account, Debit, Credit, Description, Cost Center, Profit Center Stock Item, Warehouse, Quantity, Unit Cost, Batch No, Expiry Date Open Invoices Party Type, Party, Document Type Invoice / Advance , Document No, Document Date, Due Date, Amount, Description What happens in the books All dated on the opening date: GL : one entry with your rows; the difference goes to Clearing. Stock : the stock comes in at your cost Dr each item's Inventory account, Cr Clearing . Open Invoices : one entry per party on its control account, each document kept with its own number, date and due date, so payments can be allocated against it like any invoice. Inventory, Trade Payables and Trade Receivables are not entered on the GL tab: their balances come from the Stock and Open Invoices tabs. Corrections A posted batch can be Reversed as a whole Admin, any time , then a corrected one posted. A reversal is refused when a document in it has already been paid, or the stock has since been used; undo those first. Good to know Amounts are in the default currency; quantities in the item's base unit. Dates in the paste may be dd/mm/yyyy or yyyy mm dd; at most 2,000 rows. The opening date and clearing account are fixed while any batch is posted.

pages.title: Journal Entries (JV)
pages.summary: Record any accounting entry by debits and credits: accruals, corrections, reclassifications, write-offs.
pages.text: Journal Entry Processing (JV) What it is for A Journal Voucher JV records an entry directly in the accounts: debit and credit lines that must balance. Use it for anything no other screen records: accruals and provisions, corrections, reclassifications, discounts and write offs, settling an advance against a bill. For money in or out of a cash or bank account, use Cash and Bank Transactions cash and bank.html instead. Before you start The accounts exist and are postable see Chart of Accounts chart of accounts.html . Expense, revenue and cost of sales lines need a cost center . Step by step 1. Open Journal Entry Processing JV and select New Journal Entry . 2. Fill the header: Company , Entry Date , Description , and if used the Reference , Division , Branch , Cost Center and Profit Center the header's cost and profit centers are the lines' defaults . 3. Add the lines: Account Code , Debit or Credit , description, and the cost or profit center where needed. You can paste lines from Excel into the grid. 4. A line on a vendor's or customer's account needs the Vendor / Customer , and its Allocate see Paying and allocating payments and allocation.html . 5. Check that total debits equal total credits. 6. Save as Draft to finish later, or Post Entry . Where an approval is set up, the entry goes for approval instead see Approvals approvals.html . Correcting a posted entry A posted entry can't be edited. Select Reverse Entry , choose the reversal date in an open month : a mirror entry is posted and the original stays on record. Then enter the right one. The description of a posted entry can still be corrected with the edit button next to it. Entries posted by other screens invoices, cheques, payroll, opening balances… are reversed from their own screen; the JV screen refuses them and says where. What happens in the books When posted, each line is recorded on its account and date, and the entry gets its numbers: the JV number per company and year and the Txn Ref the finance reference, shared with other finance documents . It shows in the General Ledger general ledger.html , Trial Balance trial balance.html and the statements. Rights Viewing, drafting and posting are separate rights Roles & Permissions . Approval, where set up, is by the approvers in Approval Configuration. Questions and mistakes "…is closed for …" : the entry date is in a closed month. Use a date in an open month, or ask for the month to be reopened Period Closing period closing.html . A cost center is required : expense, revenue and cost of sales lines need one. A party is required : a line on a vendor's payables or customer's receivables account must name that party, and only that party's own account may be used.

pages.title: Cash and Bank Transactions (CBT)
pages.summary: Payments, receipts and transfers through cash and bank accounts, with vendor and customer allocation.
pages.text: Cash and Bank Transactions (CBT) What it is for Records every movement through a cash or bank account: Type Use it for Bank Payment / Cash Payment Paying a vendor, an expense, an advance Bank Receipt / Cash Receipt Money received from a customer or anyone else Fund Transfer Moving money between your own cash and bank accounts Before you start Your cash accounts codes starting 10 and bank accounts codes starting 11 in the Chart of Accounts chart of accounts.html . Vendors and customers set up with their payables / receivables account. Step by step 1. Open Cash and Bank Transactions and select New Transaction . 2. Choose the Transaction Type , then the Company . 3. Choose the Ledger Account : the cash or bank account the money moves through for a Fund Transfer, the account it moves from . 4. Fill the date, description and reference. 5. Add the other side, one line per account: who it was Paid To , Received From , or for a transfer the account it goes To ; the Amount , a description, and a cost center where the account needs one. 6. For a vendor or customer, pick the Vendor / Customer and Allocate the amount to their bills see Paying and allocating payments and allocation.html . 7. Save as Draft , or post. Where an approval applies to that transaction type, it goes for approval instead. 8. Print gives the payment or receipt voucher. Correcting a posted transaction Select Reverse Entry and choose the date: a mirror entry is posted and any bills it settled become unpaid again. Then enter it correctly. What happens in the books Payment: Dr each line's account e.g. the vendor's payables , Cr the cash or bank account. Receipt: Dr the cash or bank account, Cr each line's account e.g. the customer's receivables . Fund Transfer: Dr the account it goes to, Cr the account it comes from. The entry gets a Voucher No. per type and company, and a Txn Ref . Rights As Journal Entries: view, draft and post are separate rights. Approval can be set per transaction type Approval Configuration . Questions and mistakes "…is closed for …" : the date is in a closed month Period Closing period closing.html . The allocation doesn't fit : a bill was paid by someone else in the meantime; the ERP checks again when posting. Open Allocate and choose again. Post dated cheques are not entered here: use Post dated Cheques post dated cheques.html .

pages.title: Paying and allocating against bills
pages.summary: How payments, receipts and adjustments are tied to a vendor or customer and matched to their invoices.
pages.text: Why it matters Each vendor and customer has its own account payables or receivables . To know what is still owed per invoice — for statements, aging and due dates — every amount on those accounts names its party and says what it settles. The two kinds of allocation Kind Meaning Example Against Ref Settles bills or invoices already posted or an earlier advance Paying invoice VI 1021 in full and VI 1034 in part New Ref Opens a new item for the party An advance paid before any bill exists A line's allocations add up to its amount. A line with no allocation chosen is kept as a New Ref for its full amount. Step by step: a payment against bills 1. In Cash and Bank Transactions cash and bank.html Bank Payment , add a line on the vendor's payables account and choose the Vendor / Customer . 2. Select Allocate . The vendor's open items show with their date, due date and Outstanding amount. 3. Enter the amount against each bill, or select Oldest first to fill from the oldest. Clear starts again; Done keeps it. 4. Post. The bills show as Paid or Partly paid in the invoice lists. Settling an advance against a bill Use a Journal Entry journal entries.html with two lines on the vendor's account: one Against the bill, one Against the advance, same amount on opposite sides. Discounts and write offs A JV: the party line Against the invoice, and the discount or write off amount on the expense or income account on the other line. Good to know A party line may only use that party's own payables or receivables account. When posting, the ERP checks again that each bill still has enough outstanding; if someone else paid it meanwhile, the post is refused with the reason. An invoice can't be reversed while payments are allocated to it: reverse those payments first. Due dates are the invoice date plus the party's payment terms.

pages.title: Recurring Journal Entries
pages.summary: Entries that repeat on a schedule — rent, depreciation-like accruals, prepaid expenses spread over months.
pages.text: Recurring Journal Entries What it is for A recurring entry is a template that posts the same journal on a schedule: monthly rent accrual, a prepaid insurance spread over twelve months, a monthly provision. Each run becomes a normal journal entry dated on its run date. Before you start The accounts exist, as for a Journal Entry journal entries.html . Step by step 1. Open Recurring Journal Entries and select New Recurring Entry . 2. Fill the header and lines as on a JV. The description may include {MONTH} , {DATE} or {YEAR} for example "Rent {MONTH}" posts "Rent Oct 2026" . 3. Choose the Amounts : Fixed : the lines' amounts on every run; Spread a total : a total shared equally over the runs; Spread by service period : a total over a service period from, to , each month charged for its days; for example 12,000 for 16 Sep – 15 Sep gives 500, then 1,000 a month, then 500. 4. Choose the Schedule : monthly on a day a day past the month's end runs on its last day , monthly at month end, weekly on a weekday, or monthly on the first … last weekday; every 1, 2, 3… months or weeks 3 = quarterly, 12 = yearly . 5. Choose when it Ends : on an end date, or after a number of runs. 6. Check the preview: every run date with its amount. 7. Save , then activate it with approval, where set up . Posting the runs Runs are posted by a person, not automatically. When a run's date comes, Recurring Journal Entries Due to Post appears in Home tasks. Select Post Due Runs on the list for all, or on one entry . Missed past dates are posted each with its own date. Run by run On an entry's run list: Skip a date no posting that month ; Reverse a posted run a mirror entry; then Post again or Skip ; a run that failed an account made inactive, a closed month… shows the reason; fix it and post again. Changing an active entry Pause , edit, then resume it goes through approval again where set up . End stops it for good. What happens in the books Each run posts a journal entry numbered RJV … dated on its run date, seen in the General Ledger like any JV. Reverse runs from this screen, not from the JV screen. Rights As Journal Entries; activating, pausing, ending, skipping and reversing need the post right.

pages.title: Post-dated Cheques (PDC Received and Issued)
pages.summary: Cheques dated in the future: received from customers or issued to vendors, then cleared, bounced or cancelled.
pages.text: PDC Received PDC Issued What it is for A post dated cheque PDC settles invoices on the day you receive or issue it, but the money only moves on the cheque date. These screens keep the cheque in a clearing account until then. PDC Received : cheques from customers. PDC Issued : cheques you give vendors. Before you start In Company Master , the company's PDC Received Clearing and PDC Issued Clearing accounts. The customer or vendor set up with its receivables / payables account. Step by step Record a cheque 1. Select New PDC . 2. Choose the Company and the customer or vendor. 3. Enter the date received or issued, the Cheque Date , Cheque No. , the amount and a description. Received: type the Drawee Bank the customer's bank . Issued: choose your bank account it is drawn on. 4. Allocate the cheque to the invoices it pays or Oldest first . Anything not allocated stays as an advance. 5. If it replaces a bounced cheque, choose it in Replaces . 6. Save Draft , or Post or submit for approval, where set up . Clear it on its date When the cheque date comes, the cheque appears in Home tasks under Post dated Cheques Due to Clear and in the Due to clear view. Select Clear to Bank with the clearing date not before the cheque date ; for a received cheque, choose the bank account it was deposited into. Several cheques can be cleared together with Clear Selected . If it doesn't go through Bounced : the bank returned it. Enter the date and reason; the invoices it settled are open again. Cancel Cheque : withdrawn before clearing, same effect. Undo Clearing : a clearing entered by mistake goes back to Pending. Bank charges for a bounced cheque are entered separately a JV or CBT . What happens in the books Event PDC Received PDC Issued Post Dr PDC Received Clearing · Cr the customer Dr the vendor · Cr PDC Issued Clearing Clear Dr Bank · Cr PDC Received Clearing Dr PDC Issued Clearing · Cr Bank Bounce / cancel The post entry reversed: the party owes again The same The invoices show "Paid PDC pending " until the cheque clears. Statements of account list pending cheques separately. Rights As Cash and Bank Transactions: view, draft, and post which also covers clear, bounce, cancel and undo . Questions and mistakes Refused as a duplicate : the same cheque number and bank, and party is already recorded and not bounced or cancelled. Can't clear before the cheque date. Can't bounce : an advance the cheque created has since been used against an invoice; undo that first.

pages.title: Statements of Account (Vendor and Customer)
pages.summary: Everything posted with one vendor or customer over a period, the running balance, what is still open, and pending cheques.
pages.text: Vendor Statement of Account (SOA) Customer Statement of Account (SOA) What it is for A statement of account SOA shows one vendor's or customer's history for a period: opening balance, every invoice, payment, receipt, note and adjustment with a running balance, the closing balance, and what is still open by document. Step by step 1. Open Vendor Statement of Account or Customer Statement of Account . 2. Choose the Company and the vendor or customer. 3. Choose From and To , and select Run . 4. Read it: the rows with debit, credit and balance; open items : each unpaid document with its due date, days overdue and outstanding amount, and the aging of what is open; pending PDCs : cheques not yet cleared at the end date; a check against the party's account in the General Ledger. 5. Select a document number to open it Back returns to the statement . 6. Print for the party, or CSV to open it in Excel. Good to know The open items always add up to the closing balance, because every amount on a party's account is allocated see Paying and allocating payments and allocation.html . The print leaves out the internal GL check.

pages.title: Customer and Vendor Aging
pages.summary: How old each party's open balance is, in buckets, with advances and pending cheques shown apart.
pages.text: Customer Aging Vendor Aging What it is for Shows, for every customer or vendor with something open, how much is not yet due and how much is overdue by 1–30, 31–60, 61–90 or more than 90 days — to chase collections or plan payments. Step by step 1. Open Customer Aging or Vendor Aging . 2. Choose the Company and the As at date today by default . 3. Choose Age by : Days overdue from the due date : Not yet due, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, over 90; Days since the invoice date : 0–30, 31–60, 61–90, 91–120, over 120. 4. Select Run . 5. Each row is one party: payment terms, the buckets, Owed , Unapplied credits advances and credits not matched to an invoice , Net balance , and Pending PDCs shown, not deducted . 6. Select a row to see its open documents; SOA opens the party's statement statements of account.html . 7. Copy to Excel or Print . Good to know The report checks its total against the parties' accounts in the General Ledger at that date and says whether they agree. Each party's figures agree with its statement of account at the same date.

pages.title: General Ledger Report (Ledger and Listing)
pages.summary: Every line posted to an account, with its opening, running and closing balance; or a plain listing across several accounts.
pages.text: General Ledger Reports (GL) What it is for The General Ledger shows what was posted to an account and why. It has two views: Ledger : one account over a period, with opening balance, every line, running balance and closing balance; Listing several accounts : the lines of any accounts you pick, by date, without balances, with debit and credit totals. Step by step Ledger 1. Open General Ledger Reports GL , keep Ledger selected. 2. Choose the Company , the Account , From and To . 3. If needed, narrow by Division , Branch , Cost Center or Profit Center . 4. Tick Include Draft entries to see drafts as well marked DRAFT; their figures may still change . 5. Select Run Report . Listing 1. Select Listing several accounts . 2. Pick an account and select Add or press Enter ; repeat for more. A header account brings in every account beneath it. Remove one with its ×. 3. Choose the dates and filters, and run it. From a line to its source Select the Txn Ref to see the whole journal GL Impact : every line with account, cost center, debit and credit. From there, Copy to Excel or Open source document the invoice, payment, cheque… that posted it . Select the Voucher No. to open the source document directly. Copy Table and Print follow the view on screen. Good to know Reports such as the Trial Balance trial balance.html open the General Ledger for an account when you select it; Back returns. A listing shows at most 20,000 lines; narrow the dates or accounts if asked.

pages.title: Trial Balance
pages.summary: Every account's opening balance, movements and closing balance for a period, with drill-down to the ledger.
pages.text: Trial Balance (TB) What it is for The Trial Balance lists every account with its Opening balance, the period's Transactions debit and credit and its Closing balance. Total debits equal total credits; it is the first check that the books are complete. Step by step 1. Open Trial Balance TB . 2. Choose the Company and the period. From starts at the beginning of the company's financial year; change it as needed. 3. Narrow by Division , Branch , Cost Center or Profit Center if needed. 4. Select Run Report . 5. Select an account to open its General Ledger general ledger.html for the same period; Back returns here. 6. Copy Table to Excel, or Print . Before year end closing After a financial year is closed, its income and expense accounts are zeroed into Retained Earnings by the year end closing entry. Tick Before year end closing to see the closed year's income and expense balances as they were. Good to know Anything dated before From is in the Opening column. See Period Closing period closing.html for the year end entry.

pages.title: Profit and Loss, Balance Sheet and Cash Flow
pages.summary: The three financial statements, with drill-down from each figure to the ledger.
pages.text: Profit and Loss Statement (P&L) Balance Sheet (BS) Cash Flow Statement (CFS) What it is for Statement Shows Period Profit and Loss P&L Revenue, cost of sales and expenses, and the profit From – To Balance Sheet Assets, liabilities and equity As of a date Cash Flow Statement Cash in and out, by Operating, Investing and Financing From – To Step by step 1. Open the statement and choose the Company . 2. Choose the period From and To or, for the Balance Sheet, the As Of date. 3. Narrow by Division , Branch , Cost Center or Profit Center if needed for example a P&L per cost center . 4. Select Run Report . 5. Select an account line to open its General Ledger general ledger.html ; Back returns. 6. Copy Table to Excel, or Print . Good to know The P&L leaves out the year end closing entry, so a closed year still shows its profit. The Cash Flow is by the direct method: each cash or bank movement is classed by the account on its other side. That account's Cash Flow Category comes from its header in the Chart of Accounts chart of accounts.html ; without one it counts as Operating. The figures follow the posted entries only; drafts are not included.

pages.title: Period Closing (month-end and year-end)
pages.summary: Check and close each month so nothing more can be posted into it, and close the financial year into Retained Earnings.
pages.text: Period Closing What it is for Closing a month locks it: nothing can be posted, reversed or approved with a date in it, so reported figures stay as reported. Closing the year moves its profit or loss into Retained Earnings. Before you start On the Setup tab, per company: the Financial year : January – December or April – March fixed after the first year end ; the Retained Earnings account ; the checklist : each item set to Block the month can't close while it finds something , Warn listed, but the month can still close or Off not checked . Checklist item Drafts dated in the period, not posted Documents waiting for approval Recurring journals due and not posted Depreciation not run for the month Payroll for the month not posted Post dated cheques matured and not cleared Customer Aging agrees with the receivables accounts Vendor Aging agrees with the payables accounts Stock value agrees with the inventory accounts The Trial Balance balances Step by step Close a month 1. Open Period Closing , choose the Company ; the Months grid shows the year. 2. On the first open month, run the Checklist : each item shows what it found, with the documents. 3. Fix what blocks, then select Close . Months close in order. Reopen a month Select Reopen on it and give the reason. The months after it reopen too; the ones before stay closed. Every close and reopen is in the Log . Close the year When all twelve months are closed and the previous year is closed , select Close the year . After you confirm, a Year End Closing entry YEC … dated on the last day of the year moves every income, cost of sales and expense balance, by account and cost center, to Retained Earnings. Reopen the year with a reason reverses that entry; a month of a closed year can't be reopened until its year is. What happens in the books Closing a month posts nothing. Closing the year posts the Year End Closing entry. The P&L financial statements.html leaves it out; the Trial Balance trial balance.html can show the year before it. Payroll and depreciation in a closed month Reversing or redoing a payroll run, a settlement, a loan or depreciation of a closed month offers to date it in the first open month instead; the entry records the original date. Rights Viewing and the checklist: Period Closing access. Closing and reopening are separate rights by default Admin and Finance Manager . Questions and mistakes "yyyy mm is closed for …" on any screen: the document's date is in a closed month. Use an open month's date, or reopen the month here. Can't close : a blocking checklist item found something; open it to see the documents.

pages.title: Procurement Setup
pages.summary: Set the company buying defaults that govern requisitions, orders and receiving.
pages.text: Procurement Setup What it is for Procurement Setup defines the standard company buying rules. It keeps the same defaults across all purchases, so requisitions, orders and receipts follow the same purchasing controls. Before you start The company is already created and the relevant accounts exist in the Chart of Accounts. The purchasing team has agreed which approvals and controls the company uses. The item and supplier setup is ready before the workflow is released to users. Step by step 1. Open Procurement Setup and select the company. 2. Review the default approval and receiving rules used for the company. 3. Confirm the purchase defaults that should apply to new requisitions and orders. 4. Save the setup and test a simple requisition or order to confirm the rules are active. What happens in the books Procurement Setup does not post entries by itself. It determines the defaults the ERP uses when the actual requisition, purchase order, GRN and invoice are created. Rights This screen is normally restricted to the ERP administrator or the procurement setup role. Questions and mistakes If the expected rules are not showing, the company or role setup may be incomplete. If the flow is blocked at the next step, check whether the setup was saved and the company is selected correctly.

pages.title: Vendor Master
pages.summary: Maintain the supplier record used in requisitions, purchase orders, GRNs and supplier bills.
pages.text: Vendor Master Data What it is for Vendor Master keeps every supplier record used by the buying process. The ERP reuses this record when a purchase is raised, received and finally invoiced. Before you start The company and the vendor account structure are set up in the ERP. The vendor's tax and company details are known. If the company wants supplier controls, the approval and payment rules are already defined. Step by step 1. Open Vendor Master and choose the company. 2. Add or update the vendor's basic details: name, address, contact and tax information. 3. Complete the trade details needed for purchasing and payment processing. 4. Save the vendor and test a PO or GRN using that vendor. What happens in the books Vendor Master stores the supplier identity used by the purchase flow. The actual accounting impact appears later when the supplier bill and any related payments are posted. Rights Typically a procurement or master data role can maintain vendors. Full setup rights are usually limited to admin or finance support users. Questions and mistakes If a vendor is missing from the dropdown, the record may not be saved or the company filter may be wrong. If a supplier bill cannot be matched, check that the company and vendor on the PO and GRN are the same supplier record.

pages.title: Purchase Requisition
pages.summary: Ask for a purchase before the order is raised, with approval and tracking for the requested item or service.
pages.text: Purchase Requisition What it is for Purchase Requisition is the request for stock or a service before a vendor order is issued. It creates a formal record and allows approval before purchasing begins. Before you start The company, vendor and item setup are in place. The approval workflow is configured for requisitions. The requestor knows the quantity, description and date needed. Step by step 1. Open Purchase Requisition and choose the company. 2. Enter the request header and the requested lines. 3. Add the quantities, units and descriptions needed. 4. Submit the requisition. Where approval is configured, it goes to the approver. 5. Once approved, create the purchase order from the approved request. What happens in the books A requisition does not post to the general ledger. It is a control and approval document, not an accounting entry. Rights Users need approval and draft rights for the requisition workflow, and approvers need the approval role for the module. Questions and mistakes The requisition can be rejected or returned for correction. If the item is not available for selection, check the item master and the company assignment.

pages.title: Inventory Purchase Requisition
pages.summary: Raise a stock requisition for inventory needs before the warehouse buys and receives the goods.
pages.text: Inventory Purchase Requisition What it is for Inventory Purchase Requisition is the stock specific version of a purchase request. It is used when a warehouse or department asks for a stock purchase before a supplier order is raised. Before you start The stock item and warehouse details are known. The item is in Item Master and is active for purchase. The workflow and any approval steps are ready. Step by step 1. Open Inventory Purchase Requisition and choose the company. 2. Add the item, quantity and warehouse or location. 3. Add any notes for the purchasing team. 4. Submit it for approval when required. 5. When approved, it can be used to raise the purchase order. What happens in the books This requisition still does not post a financial entry; it is a control document that prepares a future stock purchase. Rights Requestors need access and draft rights. Approvers need the approval right for the requisition. Questions and mistakes If a warehouse does not appear, the warehouse or company setup may be incomplete. If a stock item is not available, check its item master and item status.

pages.title: Purchase Order
pages.summary: Issue the approved order to the supplier and keep the commitment, delivery and receiving status aligned.
pages.text: Purchase Order What it is for Purchase Order is the supplier commitment that follows an approved requisition or a direct vendor request. It formalises the quantity, price and delivery plan for the goods or service. Before you start The supplier has a valid vendor record. The item and quantity are approved. The order date and delivery target are known. Step by step 1. Open Purchase Order and choose the company. 2. Select the supplier and the items or services to order. 3. Confirm the quantity, prices, delivery date and warehouse. 4. Submit it. If configured, it goes for approval before the order is active. 5. Track the order until receipt or closure. What happens in the books A purchase order itself is usually a commitment document, not a stock or ledger entry. The real accounting effect happens when the goods are received and the invoice is posted. Rights Users need access and draft rights to create orders, and approval rights if approval is enabled. Questions and mistakes If quantities or suppliers do not line up, check the approved requisition or vendor record. If the order cannot be completed, the company or item configuration may not be valid for the selected supplier.

pages.title: Goods Receipt Note (GRN)
pages.summary: Receive the purchased goods into stock and match the supplier receipt against the order.
pages.text: Goods Receipt (GRN) What it is for Goods Receipt Note GRN records what actually arrived from the vendor. This is where the ERP turns a purchase order into real stock on hand. Before you start The purchase order is approved and open. The item, supplier and warehouse are valid. The company has the right stock account and GRN settings. Step by step 1. Open Goods Receipt Note and select the company. 2. Choose the supplier and the approved purchase order. 3. Enter the received quantities, item by item. 4. Check the warehouse, unit and any batch or expiry details. 5. Post the GRN. The stock ledger and item availability update with the receipt. What happens in the books The GRN updates the stock ledger and the item value basis. It is also the document the supplier invoice will match against later. Rights Users need access and post rights to receive stock against a purchase order. Questions and mistakes If the item does not appear, check the PO or item master. If the receipt is refused, the supplier or order details may be mismatched. A closed month will reject a GRN date in the closed period.

pages.title: Vendor Invoice
pages.summary: Match the supplier bill to the received GRNs and post the payable amount to the company books.
pages.text: Vendor Invoice Processing What it is for Vendor Invoice records the supplier bill against the received goods or services. It checks the invoice against the GRNs and records the payables impact in the ledger. Before you start The GRN is posted and the purchase is received. The supplier and company match the PO and GRN. The invoice amount and quantities are ready for verification. Step by step 1. Open Vendor Invoice and choose the company. 2. Choose the supplier and the relevant GRNs to match. 3. Review the items, quantities and amounts before posting. 4. Save or post the vendor invoice once the supplier bill is confirmed. 5. Review the payables impact in the ledger. What happens in the books The vendor invoice records the supplier liability and clears the matched purchase value from the receiving side. This is the main point where the purchase becomes a balance in accounts payable. Rights Users need access and post rights for supplier invoice processing; approval may be required in some companies. Questions and mistakes If the invoice is refused, the supplier, GRN or company may not match. If the amount does not tie to the GRN, recheck the posted receipt and the supplier bill.

pages.title: Purchase Return / Debit Note
pages.summary: Return goods to the supplier, reverse the stock and capture the debit note for the vendor return.
pages.text: Purchase Return / Debit Note What it is for Purchase Return / Debit Note records stock being sent back to a supplier. It reverses the value and quantity taken from the original purchase and keeps a record for the supplier's debit note. Before you start The original invoice or GRN is still valid for return. The supplier and company details are known. The item quantity being returned is confirmed and the reason is recorded. Step by step 1. Open Purchase Return / Debit Note and choose the company. 2. Select the vendor and the source invoice or GRN line. 3. Enter the return quantity and the reason for the return. 4. Post the return. The system updates the stock and the supplier return ledger. 5. Review the resulting value and any variance entries created by the return. What happens in the books The return reduces stock and may create a variance if the return value differs from the original cost. The supplier balance also reflects the return or debit note. Rights Users need access and post rights for returns, plus approval rights if the company uses approval on returns. Questions and mistakes A return can be refused if the source invoice or GRN line is already fully returned or reversed. If the return value differs from the expected value, review the original vendor invoice and the stock cost used in the receipt.

pages.title: Item Master
pages.summary: Maintain the master item record used by purchase, stock movement, valuations and stock reports.
pages.text: Item Master What it is for Item Master is the core record for every stocked item. It defines the item, its stock rules, and the company data that allows purchasing and inventory movement. Before you start The item category and units are already set. The company has its stock accounts and item coding rules. The item is active for the relevant warehouse and company. Step by step 1. Open Item Master and choose the company. 2. Add or edit the item record: code, description, unit and category. 3. Set the stock and cost details required by the company. 4. Save the item and check it appears in the stock routines. What happens in the books The item master does not create a ledger entry itself. It provides the item definition that the purchase, stock issue, transfer and valuation processes use. Rights Users need write access for item setup. Read access is often broader than write access. Questions and mistakes If an item does not appear on a stock screen, check the item status and the company assignment. If the item has no cost basis, the system will not post a trade movement correctly.

pages.title: Units of Measure
pages.summary: Define the units used by stock transactions and reporting, including conversions where needed.
pages.text: Unit of Measure What it is for Units of Measure UOM defines how quantities are represented in the ERP and how one unit converts to another. Before you start The team knows the real handling units used by the business. The item categories are already planned. Step by step 1. Open UOM . 2. Add the base units used by the business and the conversion rules between them. 3. Save and test the unit on a simple item or stock transaction. What happens in the books UOM controls the quantity and conversion basis used by stock movements and reports. It does not post a journal entry on its own. Rights This screen is usually restricted to admin or stock setup users. Questions and mistakes A transaction can fail if the chosen unit is not valid for the item. Conversion mismatches are common, so check each unit before posting stock.

pages.title: Item Sub Category
pages.summary: Group items by type or line so stock and reporting match the company’s product structure.
pages.text: Item Sub-Category What it is for Item Sub Category groups items into categories such as product line, department or stock family. This makes reporting and planning easier. Before you start The parent item categories are known. Staff agree which grouping is used for reporting and stock control. Step by step 1. Open Item Sub Category . 2. Add a group or update an existing category. 3. Save and link items to the correct category. What happens in the books This screen does not create a ledger entry. It provides classification used by stock reporting and item setup. Rights Usually limited to stock setup or admin roles. Questions and mistakes If a category is missing from the list, it has not been saved or mapped for the selected company.

pages.title: Material Issue
pages.summary: Issue stock to a department or process and keep the warehouse quantity and cost records aligned.
pages.text: Material Issue (MI) What it is for Material Issue records stock leaving the warehouse for a department, project or production use. Before you start The item is active in Item Master. The warehouse and stock quantity exist. The company is not in a closed period for the issue date. Step by step 1. Open Material Issue and select the company. 2. Choose the item, quantity and warehouse. 3. Add the department or reason for the issue. 4. Post the issue. The stock ledger and available balance update. What happens in the books The issue reduces the warehouse balance and creates the related stock movement and value impact. Rights Users need access and post rights. Some companies restrict issue posting to warehouse or stock roles. Questions and mistakes A stock issue can fail if the warehouse has insufficient available quantity. If a department is not allowed, check the company’s warehouse or project setup.

pages.title: Warehouse Movement
pages.summary: Transfer stock between warehouses or locations while keeping the ledger and balances in step.
pages.text: Warehouse Movement What it is for Warehouse Movement moves stock from one warehouse or location to another without changing the overall company stock, but changing where it sits. Before you start Both warehouses or locations are configured. The item exists and the source location has stock available. Step by step 1. Open Warehouse Movement . 2. Select the source warehouse, destination warehouse and item. 3. Enter the quantity and any movement notes. 4. Post the movement and check the balances at both locations. What happens in the books The warehouse balance moves from one location to another while the stock ledger keeps the history of the transfer. Rights Users need access and post rights for stock transfer. Questions and mistakes If the movement is refused, check the source quantity and whether the destination warehouse is valid.

pages.title: Stock Adjustment
pages.summary: Correct the item quantity or value after a count, loss, damage or writing off stock.
pages.text: Stock Adjustment What it is for Stock Adjustment fixes differences between the recorded quantity and the actual stock on the floor. Before you start The reason for the adjustment is known and approved if needed. The warehouse and item are selected correctly. The date is in an open period. Step by step 1. Open Stock Adjustment . 2. Select the company, item and warehouse. 3. Enter the adjustment quantity and the reason. 4. Post the adjustment and check the updated item balance. What happens in the books The adjustment changes the stock ledger and the item balance. It may also affect the value if the adjustment is treated as a cost bearing stock correction. Rights Users need access and post rights for adjustments. Questions and mistakes If the quantity is not allowed, check the system balance and whether the item is active. If the period is closed, move the adjustment to an open date or ask for a reopen.

pages.title: Physical Count
pages.summary: Count stock physically and post the difference between the counted quantity and the system balance.
pages.text: Physical / Cycle Count What it is for Physical Count is the count process used to check the actual stock in a warehouse against the ERP balance. Before you start The count date and warehouse are selected. The count team knows what lines are being counted. The system is expected to be in an open period for the count date. Step by step 1. Open Physical Count and choose the warehouse and company. 2. Enter the counted quantities for each item. 3. Review the difference between the counted quantity and the system quantity. 4. Post the count difference if it is accepted. What happens in the books The count posts the variance as an inventory movement, correcting the stock ledger and the warehouse balance. Rights Users need access and post rights to perform and close a count. Questions and mistakes A large variance should be reviewed before posting. If a count is refused, the period or item status may not be open for change.

pages.title: Stock Availability
pages.summary: See the stock currently available by item and warehouse, including what can still be issued.
pages.text: Stock Availability What it is for Stock Availability shows how much stock is available now based on the current balances and reservation state. Before you start The company and warehouse are known. The item master and stock transactions are already posted. Step by step 1. Open Stock Availability and select the company and warehouse. 2. Choose the item or categories to review. 3. Run the report and check the quantity available for issue. What happens in the books This is a report only. It reads the stock ledger and balances and does not change the books. Rights Typically view or report access is enough. Questions and mistakes If the quantity is lower than expected, check recent receipts, issues or reserved stock.

pages.title: Stock Ledger
pages.summary: Review the full stock movement history for items and warehouses, by date and transaction.
pages.text: Stock Ledger Report What it is for Stock Ledger shows the movement history for each item, item by item, date by date. It is the main trace for stock activity in the ERP. Before you start The item is in stock and has transactions posted. The company and warehouse are known. Step by step 1. Open Stock Ledger and choose the company. 2. Select the item, date range and warehouse if required. 3. Run the report and open any transaction for detail. What happens in the books This is a read only report based on the stock ledger. It does not change stock on its own. Rights Report access is normally sufficient. Questions and mistakes If the movement list is missing a transaction, check the date filter or whether the transaction was posted in another warehouse.

pages.title: Stock Valuation
pages.summary: Value the on-hand stock by item and company using the active stock and cost records.
pages.text: Stock Valuation Report What it is for Stock Valuation shows the current value of stock on hand for the selected company and item range. Before you start Items have a valid stock basis and posted transactions. The date or period for valuation is open and selected correctly. Step by step 1. Open Stock Valuation and choose the company. 2. Select the item set and date range if required. 3. Run the report and review the value by item. What happens in the books This is a read only valuation report sourced from the stock records and posted values. Rights View or report access is normally enough. Questions and mistakes If values look wrong, check the most recent GRN, movement and adjustment posted to that item.

pages.title: Inventory Valuation
pages.summary: Review the valuation of inventory by warehouse and item range, based on the stock history and cost basis.
pages.text: Inventory Valuation List What it is for Inventory Valuation is the wider stock value view for the selected warehouse and period. Use it for valuation balance checking and review. Before you start The stock ledger is complete and posted. Warehouse and item filters are known. Step by step 1. Open Inventory Valuation . 2. Choose the company and warehouse or item range. 3. Run the report and review the inventory value. What happens in the books This report reads stock value and cost information. It does not create entries. Rights Report access is usually enough. Questions and mistakes If the valuation is materially off, review recent GRNs, issues and count adjustments.

pages.title: Inventory Aging
pages.summary: Look at older stock by age buckets so slow-moving inventory can be reviewed and managed.
pages.text: Inventory Aging What it is for Inventory Aging groups stock by how long it has been in inventory. It helps identify slow moving or aged stock. Before you start The item master and stock history are complete. The company decides which age buckets are meaningful for the operation. Step by step 1. Open Inventory Aging and choose the company. 2. Select the warehouse or item group as needed. 3. Run the report and review the aging buckets. What happens in the books This is a reporting view only. It reads stock age and quantity, and does not post to the books. Rights View or report access is usually enough. Questions and mistakes If an item looks unusually old, check for any receipt or movement that has not been posted correctly.

pages.title: Batch / Expiry Report
pages.summary: Review batches and expiry dates to see which stock is close to expiry or needs action.
pages.text: Expiry / Batch Report What it is for Batch / Expiry Report tracks stock by batch and expiry date so the warehouse can see what is near expiration. Before you start Batch or expiry tracking is set up for the item. The relevant date range or expiry threshold is known. Step by step 1. Open Batch / Expiry Report . 2. Choose the company, warehouse and item group. 3. Run the report and review the expiry dates and remaining stock. What happens in the books This is a report only. It reads the batch and stock history and does not post to the ledger. Rights View or report access is enough. Questions and mistakes If the report shows nothing, verify that the item is batch tracked and that stock exists in the selected warehouse.

pages.title: Reorder / Low Stock Report
pages.summary: Identify items below their reorder level and see any recommended purchase shortfall.
pages.text: Reorder / Low Stock Report What it is for Reorder / Low Stock Report shows which items need replenishment because they are below their reorder level or have a shortage against the target value. Before you start The item reorder levels are set correctly in Item Master. The company uses a warehouse or stock range that matches the operational flow. Step by step 1. Open Reorder / Low Stock Report . 2. Choose the company and the warehouse or stock range. 3. Run the report and review the items that need action. What happens in the books This report is for planning and purchasing. It does not create or post stock entries by itself. Rights Read or report access is normally sufficient. Questions and mistakes If the report shows no low stock, check whether reorder levels were set and whether the current stock figures are up to date. If the stock is low but no order is created, confirm the operational process for raising the purchase request or PO.

pages.title: Customer Master
pages.summary: Keep each customer record complete so sales orders, delivery notes and customer invoices can be raised correctly.
pages.text: Customer Master Data What it is for Customer Master stores the customer record used by the sales workflow. It provides the identity, credit and contact details needed for sales orders, invoices and customer statements. Before you start The company and customer account rules are already configured. The sales type and credit terms are known. The customer has the address, tax and contact details required for billing. Step by step 1. Open Customer Master and choose the company. 2. Add or update the customer's basic details. 3. Complete the sales and credit information needed for invoicing and statements. 4. Save the record and test it in a sales order or invoice. What happens in the books The customer master is a setup record, not a journal by itself. It provides the identity and account references used in trade receivables and sales processing. Rights Usually a sales or master data role can maintain customers; full setup rights stay with admin or finance support. Questions and mistakes If a customer does not appear in sales screens, check that the record is saved for the right company. If the balance or statement does not match expectation, verify the customer account and sales type setup.

pages.title: Sales Invoice Setup
pages.summary: Set the default rules and accounts used when customer sales are invoiced and posted.
pages.text: Sales Invoice Configuration What it is for Sales Invoice Setup defines the company defaults for sales document processing. It keeps the invoicing rules consistent across the sales process and the trade receivables posting. Before you start The company and its general ledger accounts are set up. Tax, discount and output tax treatment are known. The sales team knows which sales types, return accounts and defaults are used. Step by step 1. Open Sales Invoice Setup and choose the company. 2. Review each default that affects invoices, credit notes and tax treatment. 3. Confirm the sales type defaults and account links. 4. Save and test with a small sales order or invoice. What happens in the books This setup does not create an entry by itself. It determines how the ERP posts customer sales and related receivables and tax entries later in the workflow. Rights Normally restricted to finance support or admin level setup roles. Questions and mistakes If invoices do not post as expected, recheck the account determination, sales type and company defaults. A missing output tax or receivables account is a common cause of failed invoice posting.

pages.title: Price Listing
pages.summary: Review and maintain the item prices and rates used for sales transactions and customer orders.
pages.text: Price Listing What it is for Price Listing shows the current sales prices used by the company. It is where price rules, customer pricing and standard list prices are reviewed and updated. Before you start The item master is complete. The company and sales type are known. The pricing policy is agreed for the customer or item group. Step by step 1. Open Price Listing and filter by item, customer or sales type. 2. Review the effective price and any discount or price basis. 3. Update the list or customer price when the commercial terms change. 4. Save and test the quotation or sales order using the new price. What happens in the books Price Listing itself does not create accounting entries. It just sets the rate the sales transaction uses when it is posted. Rights Sales managers, pricing maintainers and admin users typically have access; end users normally only read. Questions and mistakes A sales order using the wrong price usually means the item or customer pricing was not updated. If the price list is blank, check whether the item is active and whether the company filter is correct.

pages.title: Sales Order
pages.summary: Record the customer order before delivery and invoicing, with the right pricing and quantities.
pages.text: Sales Order What it is for Sales Order captures the customer's commitment to buy goods or services. It formalises the item, quantity, price and delivery plan before stock leaves the warehouse. Before you start The customer and pricing are in place. The item and stock basis are valid. The delivery date and warehouse are known. Step by step 1. Open Sales Order and choose the customer and company. 2. Add the item lines, quantity and requested price. 3. Confirm the delivery schedule and any discounts. 4. Save or submit for approval if the company requires it. 5. Use the order to create the delivery note or invoice when the goods are ready. What happens in the books A sales order is a commercial document, not a financial journal. The accounting entry is created later when a delivery or invoice is posted. Rights Sales staff need access and draft rights; approval rights are used where the company requires higher approval. Questions and mistakes If a line is missing, check whether the customer or item was entered correctly. If an order cannot be posted, verify the customer status and the item stock status or price basis.

pages.title: Delivery Note
pages.summary: Deliver the ordered goods and record the stock movement out of the warehouse to the customer.
pages.text: Delivery Note (Goods Dispatch) What it is for Delivery Note records the movement of stock out of the company to the customer. It is the link between the sales order and the customer invoice. Before you start The sales order and customer records are complete. The item and warehouse stock are available. The delivery date is in an open period. Step by step 1. Open Delivery Note and choose the company and customer. 2. Select the sales order or inventory lines to deliver. 3. Check the item, quantity, warehouse and delivery date. 4. Post the note. The stock ledger reduces the item quantity and records the issue to a customer. What happens in the books The delivery note updates stock movement and supports the later customer invoice. It usually does not create the final trade receivable posting by itself, unless the system is designed to do so. Rights Users need access and post rights for customer delivery processing. Questions and mistakes If delivery is refused, check the stock availability and delivery date. Mismatched customer or order lines usually mean the sales order or warehouse selection was wrong.

pages.title: Customer Invoice
pages.summary: Raise the customer bill and post the receivable to the company books against the delivered goods or services.
pages.text: Customer Invoice Processing What it is for Customer Invoice finalises the sale and posts the customer receivable. It matches the delivered goods or service to the sale and creates the finance entry for the receivable and income. Before you start The delivery note or sales order is complete. The customer account and sales type are valid. The invoice amount and taxes are ready for review. Step by step 1. Open Customer Invoice and select the company. 2. Choose the customer and the relevant delivery lines. 3. Review the items, quantities, amounts and tax before posting. 4. Save or post the invoice once the billing is confirmed. 5. Review the receivable impact in the ledger and statements. What happens in the books The customer invoice creates the receivable and the sales revenue or tax entries. It usually represents the formal billing step that follows the delivery. Rights Users need access and post rights for sales invoicing, plus approval if the company uses invoice approval. Questions and mistakes If the invoice is blocked, check the customer or sales type setup. If the amount differs from the order or delivery, recheck the price, taxes and quantity.

pages.title: Sales Return / Credit Note
pages.summary: Record returns from customers, reverse the sale and create the credit note to the customer.
pages.text: Sales Return / Credit Note What it is for Sales Return / Credit Note handles returned stock or a customer cancelled sale. It returns the inventory to stock and creates the document to reduce the customer's receivable. Before you start The original customer invoice or delivery is known. The customer and company details are valid. The option to return stock or reverse the sale is confirmed. Step by step 1. Open Sales Return / Credit Note and choose the company. 2. Select the customer and the original invoice or delivery line. 3. Enter the return quantity and the reason for the return. 4. Post the return. The stock ledger and receivable balance update accordingly. 5. Review the resulting credit note and any variance entries created. What happens in the books The return reduces the customer receivable and may re enter stock. It can also trigger a sales return variance if the value differs from the original invoice. Rights Users need access and post rights; some companies require approval on returns as part of control. Questions and mistakes If the return is not allowed, the original invoice or delivery may already have been reversed or closed. If the value is not expected, check whether the return is using the original sale price or a revised cost basis.

pages.title: Retail Sales
pages.summary: Process a retail transaction at the counter, settle the sale and print or record the receipt.
pages.text: Retail Sales What it is for Retail Sales is the point of sale flow for small sales at the counter. It handles item scanning, payment capture and the printed or electronic receipt when a customer buys directly. Before you start The store or counter setup is configured to the default tax and payment methods. The item master includes the retail items and price levels. Payment methods are assigned to the correct ledgers and posting rules. Step by step 1. Open Retail Sales and choose the relevant store or counter. 2. Scan or select each item and confirm its quantity and sales price. 3. Apply any discount or promotion where required. 4. Select the payment method and complete the sale. 5. Print the receipt or confirm the transaction is recorded. What happens in the books The point of sale sale posts a trade sales entry, updates stock and records the payment type for settlement, tax and receipts. Rights Counter users need access and post rights. Reporting and cashier controls may be restricted to managers or finance support. Questions and mistakes If the item cannot be sold, check the item status, barcode or price information. If payment is not accepted, review the payment methods and any company setup for the retail counter.

pages.title: HR Setup
pages.summary: Set the company HR defaults that drive employee configuration, leave rules and payroll controls.
pages.text: HR Setup What it is for HR Setup contains the employee structure and leave rules used by Employee Master, Employee Changes, Leave, and Payroll. It is a collection of setup registers, not a general policy text box: each tab has its own records and feeds particular parts of the workflow. Tabs at a glance HR Setup has seven tabs: Grades , Designations , Employee Fields , Document Types , Leave Types , Working Calendar , and Work Schedules . Each tab maintains a separate setup register; the sections below explain what belongs in each one. Grades Create one ordered grade ladder for the group. Each grade has a unique code, name, seniority level, and may have a minimum, midpoint, and maximum monthly basic salary for each company. The midpoint is a reference; payroll checks the employee's basic against the applicable minimum and maximum and reports a warning when it is outside the band. Designations Add job titles and, where useful, the grade range normally associated with each title. The range is a guide: an employee can be outside it, but the system warns HR rather than treating the range as a hard prohibition. Employee Fields Use Employee Fields for company specific information not already on the standard form. Each field is Date, Text, or Amount; can be compulsory or optional; belongs to Personal, Employment, or Other; and can be marked sensitive. If a custom field has values on employee records, its type cannot be changed; create a replacement field instead. Document Types Document Types control whether an employee document needs a document number or expiry date. Common types are provided to start; HR can add company specific types and retire types no longer used. Work Schedules Create named schedules with their weekend days and hours per working day. Schedules support different patterns, such as a Friday only weekend. An employee's schedule is assigned on the employee record and can be changed through an approved Employee Change from an effective date. Do not change the weekend on a schedule already used by employees; create a new schedule and transfer employees to it so leave day calculations retain their history. Leave Types Leave Types define whether a type is Leave or Duty, whether it uses a balance, whether dates count as working or calendar days, and rules such as half days, gender, probation, annual or per instance limits, supporting document thresholds, and HR confirmed returns. For balance bearing leave, configure entitlement rows by grade level and completed years of service, the carry forward cap, and pay rule rows by grade level and day number. Pay may be full salary, basic only, selected fixed earnings, a percentage, or unpaid. Cover every applicable grade and day/service range: the setup displays gaps, and the Leave Register refuses a request when no applicable rule exists. Working Calendar The Working Calendar is separate for each company. It contains weekend days and public holiday date ranges. The employee's work schedule determines their weekend; company holidays still apply to them. Before you start The company, legal entity and departments are already set up. HR and Finance have agreed the grade ladder, salary bands, leave entitlement, leave pay, and working patterns. Pay elements exist before leave pay rules use selected elements. Company calendars and any different employee work schedules are known. Treat changes as policy changes: validate the rules against representative employee cases before making them active for operational use. Step by step 1. Build the grade ladder first; set pay bands for every relevant company. 2. Add designations and their normal grade ranges. 3. Define employee fields and document types before entering employees, especially any compulsory or sensitive fields. 4. Create work schedules and confirm the company weekend and hours per day. 5. Configure Leave Types. Save a new type first, then add its pay rules and, if it uses a balance, entitlements and carry forward cap. 6. Review the warning panel for uncovered grade levels or day/service ranges and close every gap. 7. Set each company's Working Calendar, including weekend and holiday ranges. Copying a previous year's holidays is a starting point; verify the new year's dates. 8. Test using employees at different grades and service lengths, including a leave request that crosses a pay rule band and a working calendar holiday. What happens in the books HR Setup does not post to the general ledger. Grades, designations, custom fields, document types, work schedules, leave rules, and calendars supply data and rules used by employee records, leave calculations, reporting, and payroll. Rights Users with HR Setup access can view setup; the HR Setup write right is needed to change it. Employees access can also permit reading setup data needed by the employee screen. Keep write access with the HR owners of these policies. Questions and mistakes Grade or designation unavailable: check that the setup record is active and that the employee's company can use it. Pay band warning: compare basic salary with that company's band; the warning is a review prompt, not an automatic salary change. No leave entitlement or pay rule: inspect the displayed grade/service/day gaps and add a non overlapping row that covers the employee. Leave days differ from expectation: check the leave type's Working or Calendar setting, the employee's schedule, company holidays, and half day settings. A used schedule's weekend needs changing: add another schedule and use Employee Change with an effective date; editing the used weekend would change day count behavior. A custom field type needs correction: if any employee already has a value, the field type is locked. Add a new field and migrate the data deliberately. Related pages Employee Master employees.html · Employee Change employee change.html · Leave leave.html · Payroll Setup payroll setup.html

pages.title: Employee Master
pages.summary: Maintain the employee record used for payroll, leave, portal access and the employee approval flow.
pages.text: Employees What it is for Employee Master is the employee's central record for identity, employment, organization, job, manager, payroll details, documents, compensation, and history. Payroll and Leave use this record to decide which employees and terms apply in a given period. The employee number is generated using the system's employee numbering format. An ERP login and an employee record are separate records; link them only when the employee needs access to the portal or another employee linked workflow. What the record contains Personal details, contact information, emergency contact, and configured HR custom fields. Employment details: company, joining and probation dates, employment type, status, and leaving date/reason. Organization and job: division, branch, cost center the department for payroll costing , work location, grade, designation, manager, and work schedule. Bank details, IBAN, and WPS person/routing details where applicable. Employee documents, with document type, number or expiry where configured, files, renewal history, and removal reason. Compensation versions with effective dates, fixed pay elements, and agreed variable pay terms. A history of creation and subsequent corrections or approved changes. Before you start The company has active grades, designations, organization units, custom fields, document types, and work schedules in HR Setup hr setup.html . The new employee's company, joining date, job, cost center, manager, and employment details are confirmed. Pay elements and the grade's company pay band are configured before compensation is entered. Bank and WPS data are checked against the bank's requirements. Access to pay, bank details, and sensitive fields is restricted separately. Step by step Create an employee 1. Open Employees , choose New , and complete required identity, employment, job, and organization fields. 2. Choose an active grade and designation. If the designation has a usual grade range, an out of range choice is shown as a warning. 3. Assign the cost center and, if applicable, a line manager, work schedule, ERP user, and required custom fields. 4. Enter bank and sensitive information only with the appropriate sensitive right.
