Users without that right do not see protected values and cannot erase them by saving other fields. 5. Save and review the generated employee number and history entry. Maintain the record After creation, ordinary personal and contact details can be maintained under employee write access. Company, grade, designation, division, branch, cost center, and work schedule are job/organization changes: process them through Employee Change employee change.html so the change has an effective date, approval, and history. HR Setup users may use Correct for a data entry mistake, with a reason recorded in history; it is not the normal route for a promotion or transfer. Use Replace manager to move all of a departing or reassigned manager's direct reports to another manager in one operation. Review the employee's direct reports before changing a manager's status to Left. Compensation and documents Compensation is a dated version, not a single amount overwritten in place. Enter fixed monthly pay elements and agreed bonus or commission terms. Use a new effective dated version for an initial entry or correction; later job/pay changes should follow the Employee Change workflow. The basic salary is checked against the company pay band. Add documents under the employee's Documents section. Select a configured document type, enter its number/expiry when required, attach the file, and use renewal rather than replacing the old record when a document is renewed. Removal is recorded with a reason; it is not an untracked deletion. What happens in the books Creating or updating an employee does not post to the general ledger. Employee cost center, compensation versions, bank details, work schedule, and employment dates are inputs used by payroll, leave calculations, approvals, and payment files. Rights Employees access/write rights control ordinary records. The separate Employees sensitive right controls compensation, bank and WPS details, and sensitive custom fields. HR Setup write permits reasoned corrections to locked job/organization fields. Document access is controlled through employee access and the supporting document workflow. Company access limits which employees a user can see. Questions and mistakes Employee missing from a period: check company, joining/leaving dates, and status for the period. Payroll includes an employee only for months overlapping employment. Cannot change company, grade, or cost center: create an Employee Change, or use Correct with a reason only when fixing a genuine entry error. Pay band warning: confirm the basic amount and the selected grade/company band; the system flags the exception for review. Employee is missing from portal or approval routing: confirm the ERP user is linked, the manager is assigned where needed, and portal access/role settings are enabled. Manager cannot be changed to Left: reassign direct reports first with Replace manager. Sensitive field appears blank: check the user's sensitive right; a user without it cannot see the saved value. Document expiry is wrong: check the document type's expiry setting and update the document record through renewal rather than overwriting its history. Related pages HR Setup hr setup.html · Employee Change employee change.html · Employee Requests employee requests.html · Payroll Run payroll run.html

pages.title: Employee Change / Update
pages.summary: Record changes to an employee’s status, pay, roles or department while keeping the payroll and approvals aligned.
pages.text: Employee Changes What it is for Employee Change is the controlled, effective dated workflow for a promotion, increment, or transfer. It preserves the before and after values, change reason, approval decisions, and the date the new job or pay takes effect. Use it for a real employment change, not to correct a typo. A one off data entry correction is made from Employee Master with Correct and a reason; that action is restricted to HR Setup writers and remains in the employee history. Before you start The employee exists and is not marked Left. The new grade, designation, organization assignment, schedule, and/or compensation are approved in principle. The effective date and written reason are known. HR has configured the grades, designation ranges, pay bands, work schedules, and pay elements in HR Setup hr setup.html and Payroll Setup payroll setup.html . Approval Configuration for Employee Changes is ready if the company requires approvals. Step by step 1. Open Employee Changes from the employee record or the Employee Change module and choose the employee. 2. Select the document type: Promotion changes grade or designation; pay may also change. A grade promotion must move to a higher level. Increment changes pay while keeping job and organization unchanged. Transfer changes company, division, branch, cost center, or work schedule while keeping grade and designation unchanged. 3. Enter the effective date and reason. For compensation, enter the new fixed pay element amounts and terms. A percentage raise can be applied to the basic; review the calculated monthly increase. 4. Review the validation warnings, including designation grade range and company pay band warnings. Check the “before” and “after” summary carefully, especially for a company transfer. 5. Save as a draft, then submit. The configured approvers act in order; a rejected change can be corrected and resubmitted. 6. After approval, verify the employee's current job and compensation history. A future dated job/organization change is applied when its effective date arrives; a future schedule is recorded from that date so leave uses the right working days. What happens in the books The change document does not post a journal. An approved pay change creates a new compensation version effective from its date; payroll uses the version in force for each month and can calculate arrears when a change is approved after its effective month was already posted. Approved job and organization changes update the employee record on the effective date. The Employee Change number and history remain available for audit. Rights Employee Changes access is needed to view documents. Its draft right prepares and submits them; approvers are assigned through Approval Configuration. Pay details are visible to users with the Employees sensitive right and to the change's approvers. Company access still applies. Questions and mistakes A second change cannot be opened: only one Draft, Pending Approval, or Rejected change may be open for an employee. Finish, delete, or resolve it first. Promotion refused: it must change grade or designation; a grade change must move to a higher level. Increment refused: it must change compensation only. Use Promotion or Transfer for job/organization changes. Transfer refused: it must change company, division, branch, cost center, or schedule, without changing grade/designation. Pay date refused: a new pay version cannot begin on or before the latest pay version's start date. Approved change not visible yet: check its effective date. Future dated job/organization changes do not take effect early. Pay values are hidden: grant the sensitive right only to people who need access; approvers can see the pay on the document they must decide. Related pages Employee Master employees.html · HR Setup hr setup.html · Payroll Run payroll run.html · Approvals approvals.html

pages.title: Leave
pages.summary: Register and approve leave so balances, attendance and payroll deductions remain accurate.
pages.text: Leave Register What it is for Leave is the employee leave register. It calculates the days, applicable pay treatment, balance effect, document requirement, and expected return for each entry; after approval, these day level records feed the monthly leave close and payroll. Before you start Employee, grade, work schedule, and company assignment are current. HR Setup has complete Leave Type, entitlement, pay rule, and Working Calendar configuration. Approval Configuration is set up if approval is required. Portal requests also need employee/manager links and portal access. The dates, reason, and any required supporting document are available. Step by step Enter and review leave 1. Open Leave, or start from the employee's leave card. Select the employee and leave type. 2. Enter the first and last dates, and mark a half day at either end if the type allows it. Enter the reason and attach any supporting file. 3. Review the live preview before saving. It shows counted days, pay treatment by day band, balance before/after, and any portion beyond an available balance that will be unpaid. 4. Save the document. Submit it for approval; if no approval is configured, submission approves it immediately. A portal leave request first goes to the line manager and then follows the configured approval flow. 5. The approver checks the dates, balance, pay breakdown, reason, and any document flag, then approves or rejects with a reason. Record the return or adjustment For a leave type that requires HR to confirm return, record the actual return date when the employee comes back. An early return removes the unused future days from the leave and restores the balance. If the employee returns late, record the return; the extra working days are recorded as unpaid absence. Use the employee leave card to make a balance adjustment only for a documented correction, such as a verified opening balance or earned entitlement correction. Include the reason; an adjustment is not a substitute for entering the leave itself. Month and year close At month end, review the leave summary and resolve Draft or pending leave dated up to the close date. Lock months in order. The lock records the summary and monthly accruals used by payroll. Reopen only the latest locked month, with a reason, and only while its payroll run is still Draft. At year end, review the preview of balances, carry forward caps, and lapses before confirming the leave year close. What happens in the books Leave entry, approval, return, and balance adjustment do not directly post a GL journal. The approved day lines affect available balances and monthly payroll: paid leave may reduce selected pay elements or apply a percentage; unpaid leave, absence, and partial leave affect salary deductions. Monthly leave close locks the rows payroll will use. If a closed month's leave is entered later, its pay effect is assigned to a later open month as an adjustment. Rights The Leave module's access right controls visibility; draft allows entry; post allows submit/cancel/close actions; lock controls month and year close; reopen controls reopening a locked month. Approval decisions are limited to the configured approvers. Employees and line managers use their portal workflow where enabled. Company access is enforced. Questions and mistakes Working day leave starts or ends on a day off: use the employee's schedule and company holiday calendar; working day leave must start and finish on counted working days. No leave pay rule: add a non overlapping HR Setup rule covering the employee's grade and the leave day band. Leave exceeds the available balance: the excess is split off as unpaid; verify the opening balance, accrued days, adjustments, previous approved/pending bookings, and carry forward. Supporting document expected: attach it or let the approver explicitly accept the leave without it. A missing document is recorded for reporting. Leave is blocked by overlap: review the employee's existing draft, pending, or approved leave across the date range. Month cannot be locked: settle or delete leave still in Draft or pending for dates up to the applicable close date, and lock months in sequence. Month cannot be reopened: only the latest locked month can be reopened, and not after its payroll has left Draft or December's leave year has closed. Related pages HR Setup hr setup.html · Leave Reports leave reports.html · Payroll Run payroll run.html · Employee Requests employee requests.html

pages.title: Leave Reports
pages.summary: Review leave balances, absences and managerial follow-up across the company or department.
pages.text: Leave Reports What it is for Leave Reports provides four different views for operational follow up: leave balances as of a date, the approved leave register for a period, absence only records, and a monthly calendar showing who is away. Before you start Leave Types, employee grades, work schedules, and company calendars are configured. The user has Leave Reports access and company access to the data required. Choose the appropriate report view and its date/month before running it. Step by step Balance report 1. Choose an as of date and run the balance report. 2. Review each employee and balance bearing leave type. The columns separate opening balance, accrued, adjusted, taken, booked, and available days. 3. Compare the grade and service rules in HR Setup with the employee's history before requesting an adjustment. Leave register and absences 1. Select the register view and enter the period from/to dates; optionally filter by leave type. 2. Review the dates, days falling inside the selected period, unpaid days, absent days, return date, and supporting document status. 3. Use the absences view to focus on unauthorized absence and late return absence. It is a report view; correct the source record in Leave if details need changing. Who is away Choose one company and a month. The calendar marks leave by type, distinguishes pending entries from approved leave, and shades weekends/holidays. Use the away only option to reduce the list to employees with entries in that month, or show everyone for coverage planning. Copy the report where available for spreadsheet follow up. What happens in the books These are report views and do not post to the ledger or change leave records. Balances are calculated from opening balances, accruals, adjustments, and approved/booked leave. The register report includes approved records; the calendar also identifies pending leave. Rights The Leave Reports access right is separate from Leave Register access, so a reports only role can view reports without being allowed to enter, approve, or close leave. Company access still restricts the report population. Questions and mistakes No balance row: check that the employee was employed on the as of date, the leave type uses a balance, and the selected company is within the user's access. Balance is unexpected: compare the as of date, opening balance date, grade/service entitlement, adjustments, booked leave, and approved leave. A pending request reduces available balance as a booking. Register differs from all leave records: the period report includes approved leave with counted lines in that period; drafts and pending requests are not approved register entries. Calendar is unavailable for multiple companies: the calendar is run for one company at a time; select the company first. A late return appears as absence: verify the return date in the Leave Register; that screen owns the source entry. Related pages Leave leave.html · HR Setup hr setup.html · Payroll Run payroll run.html

pages.title: Payroll Setup
pages.summary: Set the company payroll account, pay elements and defaults used by each payroll run.
pages.text: Payroll Setup What it is for Payroll Setup is the configuration workspace for pay elements, payroll accounting, bank/payment file layouts, loan types, provisions, and reimbursement categories. The six tabs feed the employee compensation record, payroll calculation and posting, employee loan/claim workflows, and payroll payments. It does not calculate an employee's monthly salary by itself. It defines the elements, formulas, accounts and policies that the operational modules use. Tabs at a glance The six Payroll Setup tabs are Pay Elements , Payroll Accounting , Payment Files , Loans , Provisions , and Reimbursements . Use the matching section below for the setup maintained in each tab. Before you start HR and Finance have agreed the pay policies and the payroll accounting treatment. Companies and active, postable accounts are set up in the Chart of Accounts. Grades, bands, employee work schedules, leave pay rules, and company calendars are aligned in HR Setup hr setup.html . The bank's file specification is available if a WPS SIF or other payment file is needed. The company has assigned Payroll Setup access/write rights and Payroll/Loans/Interim/Settlement rights to the appropriate roles. Step by step Pay Elements Create each element with a unique code/name and classify it as Earning or Deduction , Fixed monthly amount on compensation or Variable entered for a payroll period , and mark the one fixed earning that is Basic. Set inactive elements out of use rather than reusing their code. Fixed elements form the employee's recurring compensation; variable elements such as bonus, commission, overtime, or one offs are entered for a period. Payroll Accounting For each company, choose the daily rate method: monthly amount divided by 30, by the actual days in that month, or monthly amount × 12 ÷ 365/366. Set Salaries Payable liability and Recoverable from employees asset , and choose how leave deductions appear in the GL: pro rata against the original earnings accounts or through the element's ledger mapping. Set the optional cut off day 1–28 if the leave month is to lock before month end; blank means after month end. For each pay element, select its shared/group GL account and any company specific override. Earnings require an expense account; deductions may post to a liability or receivable. Decide whether the fixed amount is prorated for joiners, leavers and unpaid days, and whether an earning counts in gross for leave pay/overtime calculations. For variable earning elements that represent overtime, enable the overtime formula. It can be a fixed amount per run or hours × rate. For hours based OT, choose Basic or Gross, company daily rate method or fixed divisor days, employee schedule hours or fixed hours, and a weightage. Review the displayed example against the approved company formula. Payment Files Create a format for the company and bank, either from the UAE WPS SIF starter or as a blank layout. Configure file type delimited or fixed width , delimiter/extension/line ending, filename pattern, employer and bank codes, currency/reference, and the ordered header, employee record, and trailer fields required by the bank. Enter employee WPS person ID, bank routing code and IBAN in the sensitive employee fields. Preview a posted run with an appropriate payment date, then have the bank validate the output before first live use. Loans Create each loan/advance type and select its receivable account group account with optional company override . An advance is recovered at once; a loan is recovered in instalments. Optional Employee Portal limits can cap amount in months of Basic or Gross salary and number of instalments, require completion of probation, or allow only one open request of that type. Provisions For each company, configure gratuity salary base, day rate rule, minimum service, cap, start point, service slabs, expense and liability accounts and leave salary Basic or Gross base, expense and liability accounts . Add other accruals such as flight or education: fixed annual amount or a percentage of Basic/Gross, by grade level, with company account overrides and employee exceptions. Decide whether an unused accrual is paid at leaving or lapses. Opening balances already recorded in the GL are brought in through Master Data Import, not posted again here. Reimbursements Create each employee claim category with its expense account, optional company override, monthly per employee limit, receipt requirement, and maximum age of bills. Each category has its own reimbursement pay element. Approved claims are added to the relevant month's Earnings and Deductions and paid through payroll; an over limit flag is visible to approvers, who decide whether to approve it. Finish and test Save each tab and check the selected company, group account, company override, and active status. Rehearse with representative employees and a draft run; verify the calculated lines and GL impact before approving or posting production payroll. What happens in the books Payroll Setup itself makes no journal entries. Payroll Run posts earnings, deductions, net payable or recoverable amounts, and configured provisions. Loan payout/recovery, interim payments, final settlement, and provision claims create their own entries in their respective workflows. Payment file formats only produce bank files; marking payment is the action that posts the payment accounting. Rights Payroll Setup access controls viewing; its write right controls all setup tabs. Payroll, Payroll Loan, Interim Payroll, Final Settlement, and Employee Requests have separate operational rights. Keep setup changes limited to trusted payroll and finance maintainers; they can affect all future runs. Questions and mistakes Posting account rejected: it must be active and postable, be the required account type, and belong to the group or selected company as appropriate. Pay element has no account: set its group account or company override in Payroll Accounting before posting. Leave pay or overtime gross is wrong: review the element's In gross flag, the leave pay rule, and the overtime base and divisors. Joiner/leaver or unpaid days are not prorated as expected: inspect the element's Prorated setting and company daily rate method. Payroll cannot lock leave when expected: check the company's cut off day and settle leave dated up to the cutoff first. Bank rejects the file: compare the exact field order, codes, filename, delimiters/line endings, employee WPS data, and payment date with the bank's current specification; a successful preview does not guarantee bank acceptance. Loan or reimbursement request is blocked: check the type/category is active, its account is valid, and optional limits and probation rules are intentional. Provision is missing from a run: confirm the company provision is enabled, its accounts are valid, and accrual rows cover the employee's grade level. Related pages HR Setup hr setup.html · Earnings and Deductions payroll earnings deductions.html · Payroll Run payroll run.html · Loans and Advances payroll loan.html · Provisions provisions.html

pages.title: Earnings and Deductions
pages.summary: Define the earnings, deductions and allowances that payroll calculations apply each pay cycle.
pages.text: Earnings & Deductions What it is for Earnings and Deductions is the period input register for variable pay. Payroll staff enter employee specific overtime hours or amount, bonus, commission, reimbursement, accrual payout, and one off additions/deductions for a company and month. Fixed monthly compensation is maintained on the employee's dated compensation record, not here. Before you start Payroll Setup payroll setup.html has active pay elements and their accounting/overtime rules. Employees have active records and compensation effective for the month. The payroll month and company are confirmed, and payroll input totals are approved by their source records. If an item is to be paid separately, confirm it is eligible for Interim Payroll before entering it. Step by step 1. Open Earnings and Deductions and choose the company and payroll month. 2. Add a row for each employee/variable pay element. Use employee number or employee selection, the configured element, and either hours for an hours based overtime element or an amount. Add a note to identify the source or reason; paste multiple rows from a spreadsheet when appropriate. 3. Choose Run for earnings/deductions paid through the monthly payroll, or Interim for eligible amount based earnings such as a bonus or commission that will be paid separately. Hour based overtime and accrual payouts are not paid by Interim Payroll. 4. Review the register's state: for the run, entries are included in its next calculation; interim items show whether they are awaiting a batch, in a batch, or paid. 5. Correct or remove an entry while it remains editable. Recalculate the payroll draft after changing run inputs; the run captures the input version used in its calculation. 6. For Interim items, create/select an Interim Payroll batch and include the entry. It becomes locked while reserved by a batch and is marked paid only after that payment is completed. What happens in the books Entering an item does not post a journal. Run paid inputs are included in the monthly calculation and post with that run using the element's GL account and employee cost center. Interim paid earnings post when the Interim Payroll item is paid, using a payment journal and the configured element account. Rights The PAYROLLED access right controls viewing; its draft right controls adding, editing, and deleting inputs. Company access applies. Changes to run paid rows stop once the monthly run is no longer Draft; interim rows stop being editable once included in a batch. Questions and mistakes Employee is not available: check the employee's company and employment dates; the employee must be on payroll in that month. Element is not listed: only active variable elements and available provision accrual payouts are entered here. Fixed pay belongs in compensation. Hours field is required: the overtime element is configured as hours based; enter hours, not a manually calculated amount. Run total did not change: recalculate the run after editing inputs. If the run left Draft, its run paid entries can no longer be changed; follow the run's reject/reversal controls as applicable. Entry says In the draft run/Pending approval/Posted with the run: the run owns its editability. Reopen the run to review the matching calculation and status. Interim option is rejected: only an earning paid by amount is eligible; ordinary salary, hourly overtime, and accrual payouts remain with the monthly run or provision process. Interim entry is locked: remove it from its draft batch first; after approval/payment, use the batch's payment reversal workflow rather than deleting the source row. Related pages Payroll Setup payroll setup.html · Payroll Run payroll run.html · Interim Payroll payroll interim.html · Employee Requests employee requests.html

pages.title: Payroll Run
pages.summary: Calculate and post the payroll for all employees in the selected pay cycle.
pages.text: Payroll What it is for Payroll Run calculates, reviews, approves, posts, and pays one company's payroll for a month. It combines the employee compensation version in force, payroll setup, locked leave, monthly variable inputs, loan recoveries, provisions, and any arrears or carried forward net shortfall. Before you start Employees, effective dated compensation, bank details, grades, and cost centers are current. Payroll Setup has valid element/account mappings, company daily rate settings, payable/receivable accounts, and relevant provision rules. Leave for the month is reviewed and locked in Leave leave.html . The run cannot be calculated without the locked leave month. Variable items are entered in Earnings and Deductions payroll earnings deductions.html ; loans due are active and settlements have been checked. Approval Configuration for Payroll is ready if approval is required. Confirm the month is not blocked by the accounting period lock. Step by step Calculate and review 1. Open Payroll and create/open the run for the company and month. A company has one run for a given month. 2. Calculate the run. Eligible employees are those whose employment overlaps the month. Fixed elements come from the compensation version effective for each date and use the company's daily rate method for proration. 3. Review the register totals and each employee's slip. The calculation considers paid leave rules, unpaid and absent days, duty, late leave adjustments, variable inputs, loan instalments, accrual payouts, and provision movements. 4. Investigate warnings before submission: missing compensation or IBAN, basic outside the grade band, negative net, or other employee specific exceptions. Correct source data and recalculate. 5. Recalculate whenever variable inputs or the locked leave data changes. The run records the versions it used and prevents submission if its leave lock or input set is stale. Approve and post 1. Submit the reviewed draft. If Approval Configuration requires approvals, the run becomes Pending Approval; otherwise it is approved and posts immediately. 2. Approvers review the net pay amount and employee slips, then approve or reject. Final approval posts the run. 3. Review the approved GL impact before posting where available, then verify the posted journal and run status. Posting is one payroll journal dated at the month's end, with lines clubbed by account/cost center as appropriate. Pay and issue payslips After posting, review and print employee payslips. Build/preview the configured bank file or payment list, then mark payment from the selected cash/bank account. A run can be paid in parts; track unpaid balances from its payment status. Reverse payments before reversing a paid run. Correct a posted run A posted run can be reversed only when its payments are reversed and later dependent payroll runs/settlements are dealt with first. Supply a reason, correct the source data, recalculate, and submit the run again. A closed accounting period may require the adjustment/repost to be dated in the first open month. What happens in the books Posting debits earning expense accounts by employee cost center, credits deduction accounts, and credits Salaries Payable for positive net amounts. A negative net is debited to Recoverable from employees and carried forward into a later run. Configured gratuity, leave salary, and other accrual provisions post their expense/liability movements. Loan recoveries reduce the corresponding employee loan receivable; accrual payouts reduce the provision. Payment is a separate journal that debits Salaries Payable and credits the cash/bank account. Rights PAYROLL access allows viewing runs and amounts; draft allows creating, recalculating, changing and submitting a run; configured approvers decide approval; post is used for reversal; payment rights control marking payment. Payroll amounts are sensitive: access is granted by the Payroll module and the approval workflow, while employee bank details and pay records have their own sensitive controls. Questions and mistakes Cannot calculate: lock leave for this company/month first, then inspect missing compensation, inactive elements, missing pay rules, and employee grade/schedule. Submission says recalculate: the leave month was reopened/changed or Earnings and Deductions changed after calculation. Recalculate and review the new totals. Employee absent from run: check company, joining date, leaving date, and any final settlement that is paying that month. Net differs from expectation: inspect the detailed slip by element, unpaid/paid leave, overtime formula, variable inputs, loan schedule, carry forward, arrears, and provision entries. Missing GL account or cost center: fix Payroll Setup or Employee Master, then retry posting. Expense accounts requiring cost centers need an employee cost center. Approved but not posted: inspect the posting error; a missing/inactive account can leave an approved run waiting to post. Run cannot be reversed: reverse its payments first; reverse later runs or dependent final settlements before this run. Bank file is wrong: the payment file is generated from Payroll Setup and employee WPS/bank fields. Preview and validate it against the bank format before marking payment. Related pages Payroll Setup payroll setup.html · Earnings and Deductions payroll earnings deductions.html · Leave leave.html · Interim Payroll payroll interim.html · Final Settlement payroll final settlement.html · Provisions provisions.html

pages.title: Interim Payroll
pages.summary: Run an ad hoc or partial payroll when a monthly payroll needs an interim adjustment.
pages.text: Interim Payroll What it is for Interim Payroll creates a controlled payment batch between monthly payroll runs. It pays eligible approved loans/advances, posted final settlements, and variable earnings explicitly marked for interim payment. It is not a second full salary run. Before you start The source item is ready: loan/advance is approved, final settlement is posted, or an eligible amount based earning is marked Interim in Earnings and Deductions. Employee company, IBAN/WPS details, the bank file format, payment method, and payment date are checked. Approval Configuration for Interim Payroll is set up if required; the user has draft and pay rights. Step by step 1. Open Interim Payroll and start a batch for the company. Enter the payment date and optional note. 2. Select the eligible items to include. Each item can belong to only one batch at a time; review the employee, item type, and amount before saving. 3. Submit the draft batch. It follows configured approval; with no approval set up, submission approves it immediately. Rejection returns it to Draft for correction. 4. Once approved, review the payment plan by item. Generate and inspect the configured bank file where needed, then mark each item paid from the chosen cash/bank account. 5. Confirm all items are paid and the batch status is complete. If a payment must be undone, reverse the item's payment through the batch; the corresponding item becomes payable again and the batch returns to Draft when no live payment remains. What happens in the books The approval/batch itself is not a GL posting. Payment creates the accounting entry for each item: a loan payout debits the loan receivable; a final settlement clears the settlement payable/receivable; an interim earning debits its pay element account; the cash or bank account is credited. Reversal creates mirror entries. These transactions do not become part of the monthly run's salary calculation. Rights PAYROLLIP access allows viewing; draft allows creating and submitting batches; configured approvers decide; pay allows marking and reversing payments. Company access and valid cash/bank accounts still apply. Questions and mistakes Expected item is absent: confirm it is approved/posted as required, belongs to the selected company, is unpaid, and is not reserved by another batch. An earning cannot be selected: only eligible amount based earnings marked Interim can be paid here; hourly overtime and accrual payouts are excluded. Batch cannot be submitted: it must contain at least one item that is still eligible when submitted. Cannot change an item: remove it from its Draft batch first. Submitted/approved batches must follow their status and payment reversal controls. Payment fails: check that the item is still unpaid, the payment date is valid, bank/cash account is active, and Payroll Setup has the item's account mapping. Bank file preview is empty or incomplete: check the format's record fields and employee IBAN/WPS data; only items set to be paid by bank appear in that bank file. Batch total differs from expected: compare its selected item list; the total is the sum of current eligible items and should be rechecked before submit. Related pages Payroll Setup payroll setup.html · Payroll Loan / Advance payroll loan.html · Final Settlement payroll final settlement.html · Earnings and Deductions payroll earnings deductions.html

pages.title: Payroll Loan / Advance
pages.summary: Manage loan and advance recovery and posting as part of the payroll cycle.
pages.text: Loans & Advances What it is for Loans & Advances tracks employee borrowing from draft request through approval, payout, scheduled recovery, and repayment. Loan types are defined in Payroll Setup; an advance is recovered at once, while a loan is recovered in instalments through payroll. Before you start Payroll Setup contains the active loan type, asset receivable account, and intended recovery policy. The employee is active, belongs to the selected company, and the amount/start month/instalment are agreed. Approval Configuration for Loan / Advance is ready if approval is required. A valid cash/bank account is available for payout, and Payroll Setup's payment file is configured if the payout will be included in an interim bank file. Step by step 1. Open Loans & Advances, select the employee and active type, then enter principal, instalment for a loan , recovery start month, and note. 2. Save the draft and submit it. The approval amount is the principal. A rejection returns it for correction; approval alone does not pay the employee. 3. Include the approved loan/advance in an Interim Payroll batch and pay it from cash/bank. The payout posts to the receivable account configured for that type. 4. Review the running balance and monthly recovery history. Payroll deducts the scheduled amount in each run, oldest due items first, but does not recover more than the employee's available net pay. 5. When necessary, use the loan schedule controls to skip a month, change an instalment from a specified month, or record an early repayment. Review the new balance and next due amount. 6. At leaving, review the balance with Final Settlement; the settlement deducts the remaining loan balance. Once a final settlement is beyond Draft, payout/repayment actions wait for that settlement. What happens in the books Payout debits the loan type's employee receivable and credits cash/bank. Each posted Payroll Run recovery credits that receivable and reduces the loan balance; early repayments use their own payment journal. A reversed payroll run restores the recovery balance. Final Settlement clears the remaining receivable when the employee leaves. Rights PAYROLLLOAN access controls viewing; draft prepares/submits loan records; configured approvers decide; pay controls payout and repayment. Payroll Setup write is required to maintain types and receivable accounts. Sensitive employee compensation remains subject to Employees sensitive access. Questions and mistakes Loan type missing: confirm it is active in Payroll Setup → Loans and the user can access the company. Approval completed but no money received: approved status is not payout; include the item in an Interim Payroll batch and mark it paid. Loan not recovered in a run: check status, recovery start month, skips/instalment changes, outstanding balance, and whether a settlement has taken control of the employee's balance. Recovery is less than the scheduled instalment: the run caps recovery at the employee's net amount; the remaining balance stays due. Receivable account error: the group account must be an active postable Asset account; a company override must belong to that company. Loan is already in another batch: remove it from the other Draft batch or finish/reverse that payment before reserving it again. Employee has a final settlement: changes and repayments are held while a settlement past Draft controls the remaining balance. Related pages Payroll Setup payroll setup.html · Payroll Run payroll run.html · Interim Payroll payroll interim.html · Final Settlement payroll final settlement.html

pages.title: Final Settlement
pages.summary: Finalise the employee’s end-of-service or exit settlement with all remaining balances and payments.
pages.text: Final Settlements What it is for Final Settlement calculates and clears the amounts due when an employee leaves. It brings together salary months not yet paid, leave balance, gratuity, other accruals, notice pay, additional pay/deductions, and outstanding loans in one effective dated exit document. Before you start Employee Master shows the employee as On notice or Left , with leaving date, reason, company, cost center, and final job/pay details updated. The leaving date has arrived; settlement cannot be submitted before that date. Payroll Setup has valid salary, provision, loan, and Salaries Payable/Recoverable accounts and any notice pay elements. Leave up to the leaving date is decided. Any salary months allocated to Payroll Run have a posted run containing the employee; months allocated to the settlement cannot have a run past Draft. Approval Configuration for Final Settlement is ready if approval is required. Step by step 1. Open Final Settlements and choose an employee on notice or marked Left with a leaving date. Only one settlement exists per employee. 2. Review the salary months listed. The leaving month is paid through the settlement; earlier unpaid months can be assigned either to a payroll run or to the settlement, subject to the sequence shown. 3. Review calculated lines for salary, unpaid/paid leave, gratuity, leave salary, accruals, loan balance, and any arrears or monthly inputs. Confirm the chosen salary basis and rates against the employee's compensation and Payroll Setup. 4. Enter notice days and choose whether notice is paid in lieu or deducted for short notice. Add other earning/deduction elements only when supported by the relevant business decision. 5. If an automatically calculated gratuity, leave salary, or accrual amount must be overridden, enter the agreed amount and a reason. Check all warnings and the final net: a positive amount is payable; a negative amount is due from the employee. 6. Save the draft and submit on or after the leaving date. The system recalculates, checks leave and salary month dependencies, and routes through Approval Configuration. Rejection returns it to Draft. 7. Final approval posts the settlement journal dated on the leaving date. Review the journal and settlement status, then create a payment from the configured bank file or cash/bank account. If sent through Interim Payroll, pay it there instead; do not pay it twice. 8. If a posted settlement is wrong, reverse its payment first, then reverse the settlement with a reason. Reversal restores loan recoveries and returns the document to Draft for correction. What happens in the books Approval posts one settlement journal dated the leaving date. It clears the amounts used from gratuity, leave salary and other provisions, posts the difference to expense, takes back any lapsed accrual provision, reduces loan receivables, and posts net due to Salaries Payable or Recoverable from employees. Payment is separate and clears the payable through cash/bank. A negative net is not paid out; it is recorded as an employee receivable. Rights PAYROLLFS access controls viewing; draft prepares and submits; configured approvers decide; post controls reversal; pay controls payment and payment reversal. Payroll Setup write is required to correct setup accounts. Company access and employee sensitive rights apply. Questions and mistakes Employee is not available: status must be On notice or Left, and the leaving date must be entered. Cannot submit yet: wait until the leaving date, decide/delete leave through that date, and resolve every salary month. A month left to its run must have a posted run with the employee; a month paid here cannot have a run beyond Draft. Salary month appears in both workflows: choose whether the run or settlement pays it. A submitted settlement later causes the payroll run to require recalculation and exclude that employee/month. Leave or gratuity amount is unexpected: check approved and pending leave through the exit date, unpaid day treatment, current compensation, grade/leave rules, company daily rate method, and provision setup. Override is refused: provide a non negative amount and a reason. Keep supporting approval evidence with the settlement. No GL account/cost center: configure the relevant payroll/provision/loan account and employee cost center before submission. Settlement is payable through Interim Payroll: a posted positive net settlement can be included in one Interim Payroll batch; do not also mark it paid directly. Cannot reverse: reverse the payment first and remove the settlement from any Interim Payroll batch. Reversal requires a reason. Related pages Employee Master employees.html · Employee Change employee change.html · Payroll Setup payroll setup.html · Payroll Run payroll run.html · Interim Payroll payroll interim.html · Provisions provisions.html

pages.title: Provisions
pages.summary: Maintain leave, gratuity and other provisions so payroll and year-end reporting stay aligned.
pages.text: Provisions What it is for Payroll provisions track employee liabilities that accrue over time, including end of service gratuity, unused leave salary, and company defined accruals such as travel or education benefits. Rules are configured in Payroll Setup; monthly provision amounts are calculated with Payroll Run and posted when that run is posted. Before you start HR/Finance have agreed the policy for gratuity, leave salary, and each additional accrual. Payroll Setup → Provisions has the applicable formula, grade rules, employee exceptions, and active expense/liability accounts. Opening provision balances already in the GL have been imported with their as of dates through Master Data Import; do not enter them again as a new GL posting. Employee grade, joining date, compensation, leave balances, and cost center are current. Step by step Configure the policy 1. In Payroll Setup → Provisions, select the company and configure gratuity: Basic or Gross base, day rate rule, minimum service, cap, start point, service slabs, and expense/provision accounts. 2. Configure leave salary on Basic or Gross and set its expense/liability accounts. Its days come from the employee's available balance plus booked days for leave types that use balances. 3. Define other accrual types with a unique code and either a fixed annual amount or a percentage of Basic/Gross. Add non overlapping grade level rules, company specific account overrides, and any employee specific value or exclusion. Decide whether the balance is paid at leaving or lapses. 4. Verify account types and company ownership. The expense account must be an active postable Expense; the provision account an active postable Liability. Review balances and claims 1. Open Payroll's provision balances for the company and review employee balances by provision. Balances combine opening amounts, posted run accruals, salary payouts, claims, and settlements. 2. Record an accrual claim when the company pays an eligible benefit from an accrual, such as an approved education or travel cost. Select employee, accrual, date, amount, and cash/bank account; retain the supporting evidence. 3. Review the generated journal and updated balance. If a claim was entered incorrectly, reverse it with a reason rather than editing its posted record. 4. At termination, review the provision amounts in Final Settlement. The settlement pays configured balances at leaving or takes back balances that lapse. What happens in the books Payroll Setup does not post. Each posted payroll run debits provision expense by employee cost center and credits the provision liability for the month's movement; a changed calculation can adjust an already provided balance. A claim debits the relevant provision liability and credits cash/bank. Final Settlement consumes the provision and posts any difference to expense; accruals configured to lapse are taken back. Opening balances imported from an existing GL are balance records only and are not posted again. Rights Payroll Setup access/write controls provision configuration. PAYROLL access controls provision balance review; PAYROLL pay controls accrual claims and reversals. Final Settlement permissions control the exit payout/clearance workflow. Company access applies. Questions and mistakes No provision movement in the run: verify the policy is enabled, the employee is included in the run, relevant grade/employee rules cover them, and both accounts are valid. Accrual amount is zero or unexpected: inspect the fixed annual amount/percentage, Basic/Gross selection, grade range, employee exception, service dates, and effective employee pay. Leave salary differs from the leave report: compare leave types that use a balance, employee entitlement overrides, approved/booked days, the as of date, and the daily rate method. Provision account rejected: expense must be an active postable Expense and provision must be an active postable Liability; company overrides must belong to that company. Opening balance doubles the liability: confirm the opening balance was imported as an as of balance already represented in the GL, not posted as a new expense/liability journal. Claim exceeds the expected balance: review prior posted runs, opening balance date, earlier claims/payouts, and whether a final settlement has taken control of the employee's provisions. Cannot make a claim or change a balance: check the Payroll pay right, company access, and whether a final settlement is beyond Draft. Final Settlement amount differs from monthly provision: the settlement recalculates on the leaving date and clears the liability actually provided; the difference is posted to expense or taken back. Related pages Payroll Setup payroll setup.html · Payroll Run payroll run.html · Final Settlement payroll final settlement.html · Master Data Import master import.html

pages.title: Employee Requests
pages.summary: Manage employee queries, claims and requests from the portal or the ERP’s request workflows.
pages.text: Employee Requests What it is for Employee Requests is the ERP side work queue for requests submitted through Employee Self Service. It brings employee queries and cases to the relevant handler, while claims and other request types continue through their own approval and payroll/accounting workflows. Requests may include a question or case, reimbursement claim, loan/advance request, payroll query, or a leave request that is initiated and tracked through the portal. This screen is for managing the request and its communication; it is not a substitute for the Payroll Loan, Leave, or payroll posting documents. Before you start The employee record is current, with company and line manager where the request type requires them. Employee portal access is enabled for the employee and the relevant roles have access to Employee Requests. The portal categories and policies are configured: reimbursement categories/pay elements, loan limits/types, and approval rules where used. The handler knows which actions belong in Employee Requests and which require the linked operational module. Step by step 1. Open Employee Requests and filter the list by company, request type, or status to find new and open work. 2. Open the request. Confirm the employee, category, submitted details, internal notes, and any supporting files before acting. 3. Add internal notes for the HR/payroll team. Keep notes factual and do not put sensitive payroll or identity details in a case that is visible to users who should not see them. 4. For a query, respond or route it to the appropriate handler and close it when resolved. 5. For a reimbursement, use the configured manager and approval flow. If approved, its category specific earning is carried into the relevant month in Earnings and Deductions and paid with payroll; the claim itself is not a bank payment. 6. For a loan/advance request, check the configured loan type and limits, then follow the approval and payout workflow in Loans and Advances payroll loan.html . 7. For leave, use the Leave Register and approval workflow for the authoritative dates, balance, and return handling. 8. Reopen or follow up requests that need more information; close only after the business action is complete and the employee has a clear resolution. What happens in the books Employee Requests itself is a workflow record and does not post to the general ledger. An approved reimbursement can become an earning input for Payroll; a loan request can become a loan document; a leave request can become a Leave Register document. Those downstream modules perform their own approvals, postings, and payment records. Rights Employee Requests access and handler rights are configured separately from portal access. The line manager, assigned handler, HR, and payroll staff should receive only the rights needed for their work. Access to employee sensitive pay/bank information remains controlled by Employees sensitive rights and the respective payroll module permissions. Questions and mistakes No requests appear: check the employee's portal access, company access, request handler rights, and whether the correct status/type filter is selected. Manager does not receive the task: verify the manager link on Employee Master and the request type's approval configuration. Reimbursement is approved but not paid: check the assigned payroll month, its Earnings and Deductions entry, and whether that month's run has been calculated and posted. Loan request is approved but not paid: approval is not payout; prepare the loan payout or Interim Payroll payment using its own workflow. Leave request and register disagree: update or decide the leave in Leave Register; the case thread is not the authoritative leave record. File or note is missing: reopen the request and inspect its attachment list and history; do not recreate a duplicate request unless the employee must resubmit. Related pages Employee Master employees.html · Payroll Setup payroll setup.html · Loans and Advances payroll loan.html · Leave leave.html · Payroll Run payroll run.html

pages.title: Fixed Asset Configuration
pages.summary: Configure the fixed asset classes, accounts and defaults used when assets are added and depreciated.
pages.text: Fixed Asset Configuration What it is for Fixed Asset Configuration defines the fixed asset structure for the company: classes, account determination, depreciation settings and the asset defaults used by the rest of the asset process. Before you start The company’s asset accounts and cost centers are defined. The depreciation policy is agreed with finance. Asset classes and categories are known. Step by step 1. Open Fixed Asset Configuration and select the company. 2. Review the asset classes and the account mapping used for capitalisation and depreciation. 3. Confirm the depreciation rate and treatment defaults. 4. Save the configuration and test it with one asset. What happens in the books This configuration does not post a document itself; it defines the accounts and rules that future asset additions and depreciation will use. Rights Usually only finance support or admin users with fixed asset setup rights can edit these settings. Questions and mistakes If a new asset cannot be capitalised, check the class, account and company defaults.

pages.title: Fixed Asset Master
pages.summary: Maintain the asset record that contains its details, class, location and book value basis.
pages.text: Fixed Asset Master What it is for Fixed Asset Master stores the asset’s identity and the settings used in accounting, depreciation and retirement. Before you start The asset class and account mapping are configured. The asset is assigned to the correct company and department. The acquisition details and useful life are known. Step by step 1. Open Fixed Asset Master and select the asset or add a new asset. 2. Fill in the asset details: code, description, class, date, value and location. 3. Confirm the capitalisation and depreciation settings. 4. Save and test by capitalising or running depreciation. What happens in the books The asset master is the source of information for later capitalisation and depreciation entries, but itself does not post a journal. Rights Asset owners and finance support usually have access; write access is more limited than read access. Questions and mistakes If depreciation does not appear, check whether the asset class and asset record are active and linked to the correct accounts.

pages.title: Fixed Asset Capitalization
pages.summary: Record the purchase or acquisition of a fixed asset and place it into service for depreciation.
pages.text: Fixed Asset Capitalization What it is for Fixed Asset Capitalization brings a purchased or self constructed asset into the ERP’s fixed asset register for depreciation. Before you start The asset master is already created or the class is known. The supplier or vendor invoice or accumulation record is ready. The account mapping is set in Fixed Asset Configuration. Step by step 1. Open Fixed Asset Capitalization . 2. Select the asset or create the asset from the acquisition entry. 3. Enter the acquisition value, date and any related cost details. 4. Post the acquisition. The asset is then available for depreciation. What happens in the books The capitalization posts the asset to the fixed asset register and moves the value from the clearing or purchase account into the asset account. Rights Finance or asset support roles generally need access and post rights for capitalisation. Questions and mistakes If posting is refused, check the class setup, clearing account and asset status.

pages.title: Capital Work in Progress
pages.summary: Track capital work under construction until it is completed and transferred into a fixed asset.
pages.text: Capital Work in Progress What it is for Capital Work in Progress tracks a project or asset under construction before it is fully ready for use. This keeps the asset value segregated until it is ready for capitalization. Before you start The project or asset class is configured. The asset under construction is assigned to an accountable class. The user knows which costs belong in the capital work account. Step by step 1. Open Capital Work in Progress and select the company. 2. Add the work in progress asset or project. 3. Record the values or costs being accumulated. 4. When the asset is ready, transfer it to the final fixed asset record. What happens in the books The balance remains in the capital work in progress account until the asset is transferred into service and capitalized. Rights Finance and asset setup roles generally maintain this area. Questions and mistakes If the transfer is not visible, check that the work in progress asset is active and linked to the correct class.

pages.title: Depreciation Run
pages.summary: Calculate and post the monthly depreciation for the active fixed asset register.
pages.text: Depreciation Run What it is for Depreciation Run calculates the monthly depreciation charge for all active assets using the company rules and asset class settings. Before you start Assets are capitalized and active. The depreciation policy and rates are configured. The reporting period is open. Step by step 1. Open Depreciation Run and choose the company and period. 2. Review the asset list that qualifies for the run. 3. Calculate the depreciation and check the amount per asset. 4. Post the run once it is approved. What happens in the books The run posts the depreciation expense and reduces the asset’s carrying value, while updating the accumulated depreciation account. Rights Finance and fixed asset support roles normally post the depreciation run. Questions and mistakes If an asset is missing, confirm it was capitalized and not retired or already fully depreciated.

pages.title: Additional Depreciation
pages.summary: Add one-off depreciation adjustments for assets with unusual or exceptional value changes.
pages.text: Additional Depreciation What it is for Additional Depreciation handles one off or extra depreciation adjustments beyond the normal monthly run. It is used when an asset’s useful life, value or impairment requires a special adjustment. Before you start The asset and its current value are known. The reason and period are approved. The asset is active and linked to the correct class. Step by step 1. Open Additional Depreciation and select the asset. 2. Enter the adjustment period and the extra depreciation value. 3. Review the resulting carrying value and any GL effect. 4. Post the adjustment. What happens in the books This creates or adjusts the depreciation expense and the accumulated depreciation balance according to the company policy. Rights Finance and asset admin users with additional depreciation rights can post this adjustment. Questions and mistakes If the adjustment is rejected, check whether the selected period is still open and whether the asset is still active.

pages.title: Asset Register
pages.summary: Review the assets in use, their values and their depreciation status company-wide.
pages.text: Fixed Asset Register What it is for Asset Register holds the list of active assets with their carrying values, depreciation history and status for the selected company. Before you start Assets have been capitalized and entered into the register. The company and period are known. Step by step 1. Open Asset Register and filter by asset class or department if needed. 2. Review the current carrying value, depreciation and life status. 3. Use the report for audits, finance review or asset management follow up. What happens in the books This is a reporting screen. It reads the asset register and does not itself create entries. Rights Read access is normally enough for most users; finance and auditors often need additional access. Questions and mistakes If an asset is missing, check whether it was entered and whether the asset was capitalised in the correct company.

pages.title: Fixed Asset Retirement
pages.summary: Retire a fixed asset when it is sold, scrapped or otherwise removed from service.
pages.text: Fixed Asset Retirement What it is for Fixed Asset Retirement records the removal of an asset from the fixed asset register when it is sold, discarded or otherwise disposed of. Before you start The asset is in the register and is active. The retirement date and proceeds are agreed. Any gain or loss account mapping is configured. Step by step 1. Open Fixed Asset Retirement and select the asset. 2. Enter the disposal date, proceeds and reason for retirement. 3. Review the asset’s net book value and gain or loss on disposal. 4. Post the retirement and verify the asset is closed off correctly. What happens in the books The retirement removes the asset from service and posts the net book value and any gain or loss to the relevant accounts. Rights Finance and asset support roles normally handle retirement posting. Questions and mistakes If the asset does not retire, confirm the asset is still active and the disposal date is in an open period.

pages.title: Job Order Request
pages.summary: Open a job order request to start production and confirm the required materials and output.
pages.text: Job Order Request What it is for Job Order Request records a manufacturing or production request before the production is released. It defines what is to be made, by when and in what quantity. Before you start The bill of materials and work centres are known. The production date and output target are agreed. The company’s production rules are active. Step by step 1. Open Job Order Request and select the company. 2. Enter the production item, quantity and required date. 3. Confirm the materials or cost basis associated with the job. 4. Submit or approve the request and move it into production. What happens in the books The job order request is a planning record. The actual production posting and consumption entries happen later when the job is processed. Rights Production planners and maintenance or admin users with job order access usually use this screen. Questions and mistakes If the job is not created, check whether the item and production setup are active.

pages.title: Bill of Materials
pages.summary: Define what a finished product is made of and how the materials are consumed during production.
pages.text: Bill of Materials What it is for Bill of Materials lists the materials, quantities and substitutions needed to build a finished item or product. Before you start The item master is complete for the finished product and the components. The company knows the standard recipe and any allowable substitutions. The production policy is agreed to maintain a standard BOM. Step by step 1. Open Bill of Materials and select the parent item. 2. Add or update the materials and their required quantities. 3. Save the BOM and check it against actual production experience. What happens in the books The BOM itself does not post. It is the recipe used during the production and consumption process. Rights Production planning or admin setup users usually maintain BOMs. Questions and mistakes If a production job is short of materials, review the BOM and whether the right version is active.

pages.title: Production
pages.summary: Post the completion of a production job and record the finished output into stock.
pages.text: Production Entry What it is for Production records the output created from a job order. It converts the planned effort and materials into a finished item that becomes available in stock. Before you start The job order and BOM are in place. The items and required quantities are known. The production date and warehouse are ready. Step by step 1. Open Production and select the job order or item to produce. 2. Review the planned output and actual quantities manufactured. 3. Enter the produced quantity and confirm the warehouse. 4. Post the production, which creates the stock movement for the finished goods. What happens in the books The production posting updates stock and creates the related value movement for the produced goods and any material consumption. Rights Production users and relevant finance roles generally need the right to create and post production entries. Questions and mistakes If stock does not increase as expected, review the production quantities and the warehouse assignment.

pages.title: Production Consumption
pages.summary: Record the raw materials consumed during production and keep the BOM and stock movement aligned.
pages.text: Production & Consumption Report What it is for Production Consumption records the materials used when a job order is processed. It matches the actual material usage against the planned BOM. Before you start The production job is active and the BOM is set. The item stocks are available in the selected warehouse. The production date and job order are confirmed. Step by step 1. Open Production Consumption and select the active job order. 2. Enter the materials used and quantities consumed. 3. Review the production variance against the planned required materials. 4. Post the consumption and confirm stock balances adjust correctly. What happens in the books Production consumption reduces the stock ledger and records the material cost used in the production process. Rights Production planners and stock or finance users with posting rights usually perform this task. Questions and mistakes If the stock balance is too high or low after posting, check whether the BOM quantities and warehouse lines were correct.

pages.title: Material Variance
pages.summary: Review material differences between standard BOM usage and actual consumption during production.
pages.text: Material Variance Report What it is for Material Variance flags differences between the standard material expected for a production job and the actual material consumed. Before you start The production job is posted or partially complete. The standard BOM is available for comparison. The actual material usage is known and checked. Step by step 1. Open Material Variance and select the production job or item. 2. Compare the planned and actual consumption figures. 3. Review the variance by material and reason. 4. Record the difference if the company expects a variance analysis or account posting. What happens in the books The variance helps explain booking differences in production cost and stock. It is often used to identify wastage, scrap or overuse of materials. Rights Production and finance staff often use this screen for variance review and sign off. Questions and mistakes If the variance is large, check whether the BOM is outdated or the actual consumption data is incomplete.

pages.title: Company Master
pages.summary: Keep the company profile, chart links and the legal defaults used across the ERP.
pages.text: Company Master Data What it is for Company Master holds the company profile and many of the legal and operational defaults that the rest of the ERP relies on, including account structure and tax related settings. Before you start The legal company information is agreed. The financial account and tax configuration is ready. The business knows which setup defaults must be shared across all modules. Step by step 1. Open Company Master and select the company. 2. Review the company information and operational defaults. 3. Set the required account links and the fields that should be shared with all modules. 4. Save and test a standard transaction against the company setup. What happens in the books Company Master is a setup record and not a posting document by itself. It provides the default company rules used by many other screens. Rights Usually restricted to ERP admin or finance support roles. Questions and mistakes If a screen cannot find the company or accounts, the company profile may not be set correctly.

pages.title: Organisation Units
pages.summary: Manage the company hierarchy, departments, cost centers and organisational divisions used throughout ERP processing.
pages.text: Organizational Units What it is for Organisation Units defines the company’s hierarchy, departments and operating units that other modules use for reporting and approval. Before you start The company structure is known and agreed. Departments or cost centers are mapped to reporting needs. Step by step 1. Open Organisation Units and select the company. 2. Add or update the departments or divisions needed. 3. Review how each unit maps to the relevant cost center or manager assignments. 4. Save and use it in a test posting or approval. Rights Admin and finance system setup roles usually manage organisation units. Questions and mistakes If a cost center or department is missing in a reporting screen, check whether the unit is active and linked to the correct company.

pages.title: User Management
pages.summary: Set up ERP users, assign roles and control which screens they can access and post.
pages.text: User Management What it is for User Management is the user configuration screen used to maintain ERP accounts, assign roles and define who can open and use each area. Before you start The person’s full user details and company assignment are known. The roles and permissions for the company are already defined. Step by step 1. Open User Management . 2. Create or update the ERP user and assign the company. 3. Link the user to the correct roles and rights. 4. Save and test their menu and module access. What happens in the books User Management does not create accounting entries. It controls access to the ERP and the functions available to each user. Rights Only admin users with user management rights should manage this screen. Questions and mistakes If a user cannot see a screen, check the company assignment, role and menu rights.

pages.title: Roles and Permissions
pages.summary: Define which roles can open, edit, approve, post or report on each module.
pages.text: Roles & Permissions What it is for Roles and Permissions controls the ERP’s security model. Each role determines what a user may open, change, approve or post. Before you start The company roles and business responsibilities are agreed. The menu structure and module list are known. Step by step 1. Open Roles and Permissions . 2. Select the role to maintain. 3. Assign the rights needed for each module, including read, write, approve and post appropriate actions. 4. Save and test the role against a user assigned to it. What happens in the books This screen does not post accounting entries. It governs access and acts as the ERP’s security layer. Rights Only admin users with role maintenance access should change permission rules. Questions and mistakes If a user is blocked from a module, review the assigned role and the specific module rights for that role.

pages.title: Tree Management
pages.summary: Build the menu tree and link each module to the right company, role and section.
pages.text: Module Tree & Navigation What it is for Tree Management is the screen used to arrange the ERP menu and link each module to the correct node, area and user access path. Before you start The business wants a certain menu layout. The module names and areas are known. Step by step 1. Open Tree Management . 2. Choose the node to move, rename or link. 3. Add the correct screen or module under the menu hierarchy. 4. Save and verify the user sees the correct menu structure. What happens in the books This is a menu and configuration screen, not a financial posting document. Rights Admin users with menu configuration rights should maintain this screen. Questions and mistakes If a module is missing from the menu, the tree link or rights assignment may not be saved.

pages.title: Approval Configuration
pages.summary: Set the approval rules by module, level and company so documents flow to the right approvers.
pages.text: Approval Configuration What it is for Approval Configuration defines who may approve which transaction type and how many approval levels are required before a document becomes active. Before you start The business approval policy and levels are agreed. The approvers and roles are already configured. Step by step 1. Open Approval Configuration . 2. Select the module and document type. 3. Set the approval route, required approvers and policy conditions. 4. Save and test the flow with a sample transaction. What happens in the books The configuration controls approval workflow and does not post accounting entries by itself. Rights Admin and approver setup roles normally manage this screen. Questions and mistakes If tasks do not route correctly, recheck the module mapping and the approver roles configured for the company.

pages.title: Approval Tracker
pages.summary: Track each approval request, see who acted and follow the current status of a document.
pages.text: Approval Tracker What it is for Approval Tracker shows the approval history for documents in the ERP. It lets users and administrators see where the document is, whether it was approved or rejected, and who acted. Before you start A document has already entered an approval flow. The approval configuration is active for that module. Step by step 1. Open Approval Tracker . 2. Filter by document type, status or employee. 3. Review the current approval step and the history of actions taken. 4. Use the view to follow up with approvers or request revisions. What happens in the books This is a tracking view only. It reads the approval data and does not post entries itself. Rights Most roles can view their own workflow status; admin roles often see the full history. Questions and mistakes If a document appears stuck, check whether the approver was assigned to the correct approval level.

pages.title: Numbering
pages.summary: Maintain the document prefixes, numbering format and automatic code generation across modules.
pages.text: Numbering What it is for Numbering defines how document references and codes are formed across the ERP, including prefixes, year markers and document size rules. Before you start The company’s document numbering policy is agreed. The ERP user knows which module ranges and codes are affected. Step by step 1. Open Numbering . 2. Select the document or master type. 3. Define the numbering format and reset or suffix rules as required. 4. Save and test the next generated document number. What happens in the books This is a configuration document. The actual document number is used when the transaction is created. Rights Admin or finance support roles usually maintain numbering settings. Questions and mistakes If a new document is using the wrong sequence, check the numbering format and the company or code that was selected.

pages.title: Master Data Import
pages.summary: Import item, supplier, customer or other master data in bulk and make the ERP updates reliably.
pages.text: Master Data Import What it is for Master Data Import is the bulk upload screen used to import or refresh master records in the ERP, often for items, suppliers, customers or employee data. Before you start The import file is prepared and validated. The mapping between the file and the ERP columns is known. The company and update mode are agreed before upload. Step by step 1. Open Master Data Import . 2. Select the import type and company. 3. Upload the file and review the mapping. 4. Run the import and fix any validation or row level errors. What happens in the books The import creates or updates the relevant master records. It does not usually create a separate finance entry by itself. Rights Admin and data support users typically have access to this screen. Questions and mistakes If a row fails, check the mapping and whether the data already exists in the ERP as a different record type or company.

pages.title: Document Storage
pages.summary: Store and retrieve supporting files for modules, documents and approvals without going outside the ERP.
pages.text: Document Storage What it is for Document Storage keeps supporting files attached to ERP records, such as receipts, notes, contracts or payment proofs. Before you start The relevant record or document is already created. The file is in a format the ERP can store and view. Step by step 1. Open Document Storage and select the relevant company or document. 2. Upload the file or review the stored attachment. 3. Confirm the document is attached to the right record. 4. Save the record and use the attachment for audit or support. What happens in the books The screen stores or retrieves files; it does not create accounting entries by itself. Rights Users with document access or the relevant module rights usually can add and review files. Questions and mistakes If a file is missing after upload, confirm the record was saved and the attachment belonged to the correct company or document.

pages.title: Company Documents
pages.summary: Maintain company documents that expire, need review, or are attached to the company file set.
pages.text: Company Documents What it is for Company Documents maintains the documents and compliance records linked to the company, including licences, certifications or supporting files that need periodic review. Before you start The company and document type are known. The expiry date or review cycle is agreed. Step by step 1. Open Company Documents and select the company. 2. Add or update the document record and expiry dates. 3. Attach the file if needed. 4. Save and review whether the record is close to expiry or overdue. What happens in the books This screen mostly maintains records and reminders. It does not create ledger postings by itself. Rights Admin, company admin and compliance or HR users typically maintain these records. Questions and mistakes If an expiry or alert is missing, check the document type and the date configuration on the record.

pages.title: Data Reset
pages.summary: Reset or rebuild data carefully when a clean start or controlled refresh is needed for a company or environment.
pages.text: Data Reset (Admin) What it is for Data Reset is the controlled reset screen used by the ERP admin when a company, ledger or data set needs to be cleared or rebuilt in a controlled way. Before you start The reset is approved by the ERP owner or admin. A backup or recovery plan is in place. The specific company or data set to reset is confirmed. Step by step 1. Open Data Reset and choose the correct company or module area. 2. Review the scope of the reset and the records that will be affected. 3. Confirm the reset request and review the warning message. 4. Run the reset only after the approval is in place. What happens in the books This screen changes the data used in the ERP. It may remove or rebuild existing entries and should always be used only with a clear control and approval process. Rights Only admin users with reset rights should use this screen. Questions and mistakes If a reset is not allowed, check whether the company or data set is protected or whether the correct admin rights are assigned.
